statement_plain: Under the referenced SCGS parameter and stochastic-oracle conditions, the expected objective gap is bounded by an initial term plus accumulated inner-error and sampling-variance terms. An alternative parameter condition replaces the diameter term by an initial-distance term. The referenced inner-iteration bound also applies.
statement_title: Expected-Error and Inner-Iteration Bounds for Stochastic Conditional-Gradient Sliding

conclusion_latex: \mathcal H_\alpha(s)=\begin{cases}\{0\},&|s|<\alpha,\\ \{s\},&|s|>\alpha,\\ \{0,s\},&|s|=\alpha.\end{cases}
scope_note: Set-valued scalar thresholding with the equality boundary preserved; the extract does not state a domain restriction on the parameter \(\alpha\).
statement_latex: For every \(s\in\mathbb R\), the hard thresholding operator is defined by \[\mathcal H_\alpha(s)=\begin{cases}\{0\},&|s|<\alpha,\\ \{s\},&|s|>\alpha,\\ \{0,s\},&|s|=\alpha.\end{cases}\]
statement_plain: Hard thresholding returns zero below the threshold, the input above the threshold, and both zero and the input at equality. The extract does not specify the allowed values of alpha.
statement_title: Hard thresholding operator

conclusion_latex: \mathbf{S}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{d})=\left\{\mathbf{x}+\alpha\mathbf{d}:\alpha\geq0,\ f(\mathbf{x}+\alpha\mathbf{d})=\min_{\beta\geq0}f(\mathbf{x}+\beta\mathbf{d})\right\}
scope_note: Set-valued mapping assigning all attained global minimizers on the nonnegative search ray; the value may be empty when the ray minimum is not attained.
statement_latex: For \mathbf{x},\mathbf{d}\in E^n, define the set-valued mapping \mathbf{S}:E^{2n}\rightrightarrows E^n by \[\mathbf{S}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{d})=\left\{\mathbf{y}:\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{x}+\alpha\mathbf{d}\text{ for some }\alpha\geq0,\quad f(\mathbf{y})=\min_{\beta\geq0}f(\mathbf{x}+\beta\mathbf{d})\right\}.\]
statement_plain: The exact line-search solution mapping assigns to a point and direction all points attaining the global minimum of the objective along the associated nonnegative ray.
statement_title: Exact line-search solution mapping

conclusion_latex: f_{\mu_2}(\bar x)\le \phi_{\mu_1}(\bar u)
scope_note: A method-specific condition comparing smoothed primal and dual objective values.
statement_latex:
Let $Q_1,Q_2$ be sets, and let $f_{\mu_2}:Q_1\to\mathbb{R}$ and $\phi_{\mu_1}:Q_2\to\mathbb{R}$ be functions. A pair $(\bar x,\bar u)\in Q_1\times Q_2$ satisfies the excessive gap condition if
\[
f_{\mu_2}(\bar x)\le \phi_{\mu_1}(\bar u).
\]
statement_plain: A primal-dual pair satisfies the excessive gap condition when its smoothed primal objective value does not exceed its smoothed dual objective value.
statement_title: Excessive Gap Condition

conclusion_latex: \frac{\operatorname{Regret}_t}{t}\leq\sqrt{\frac{2\log k}{t}},\qquad \operatorname{Regret}_t=O(\sqrt{t\log k})
scope_note: Full-information online reward maximization over the probability simplex, including the exponential update and stated regret rate.
statement_latex:
Let $\mu_s\in[0,1]^k$ be fully observed at every round, let $\pi_0=(1/k,\ldots,1/k)$, and let $\gamma>0$. In the reward-maximization convention, Hedge updates
$$\pi_s^{(i)}=\frac{\pi_{s-1}^{(i)}\exp(\gamma\mu_s^{(i)})}{\sum_{j=1}^k\pi_{s-1}^{(j)}\exp(\gamma\mu_s^{(j)})},\qquad i=1,\ldots,k.$$
This is online mirror descent on the simplex with the entropy mirror map. For horizon $t$ and $\gamma=\sqrt{2\log(k)/t}$, the stated normalized regret satisfies
$$\frac{\operatorname{Regret}_t}{t}\leq\sqrt{\frac{2\log k}{t}},$$
so $\operatorname{Regret}_t=O(\sqrt{t\log k})$.
statement_plain: With full reward-vector feedback, Hedge starts uniformly and exponentially increases each coordinate according to its observed reward before renormalizing. In the reward-maximization convention this is entropy-based online mirror descent, with normalized regret bounded by the square root of two log k divided by t under the stated learning rate.
statement_title: Hedge as Entropic Online Mirror Descent

assumptions_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},y,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k)\neq\varnothing\text{ whenever the corresponding update is executed}
conclusion_latex: x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},y,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k),\qquad i=1,\ldots,p.
scope_note: Cyclically minimizes the objective exactly over one variable block at a time; the method is defined only when every required block argmin is nonempty.
statement_latex:
Let $E=E_1\times\cdots\times E_p$ and $F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]$. Choose $x^0=(x_1^0,\ldots,x_p^0)\in\operatorname{dom}F$. For $k=0,1,2,\ldots$, visit $i=1,\ldots,p$ in order and select
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},y,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k).
\]
Earlier blocks therefore use their new values, while later blocks retain their values from iteration $k$. If any displayed argmin is empty, the exact alternating-minimization update is not defined at that stage.
statement_plain: Start from a point in the effective domain and visit the blocks cyclically. At each visit, replace the selected block by an exact minimizer with previously visited blocks fixed at their new values and unvisited blocks fixed at their old values. The exact method is not well defined if a required block subproblem has no minimizer.
statement_title: Cyclic exact alternating minimization

conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k)
scope_note: Basic deterministic gradient iteration using a constant step size.
statement_latex: Given a differentiable objective \(f\), a fixed learning rate \(\alpha\), and a current iterate \(x_k\), compute \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha g_k\).
statement_plain: At each iteration, evaluate the gradient and subtract the fixed learning rate times that gradient from the current iterate.
statement_title: Fixed-Step Euclidean Gradient Descent

assumptions_latex: f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^r\ell_j(a_j^\top x-b_j)\text{ with differentiable closed proper convex }\ell_j\text{ for the maintained-state realization}
conclusion_latex: \text{The extract states convergence of the selected-block gradient iteration and an }O(rn_{i(k)})\text{ maintained-state implementation under the corresponding assumptions.}
scope_note: The extract states convergence but does not specify the block-sampling law or convergence mode. Its structured-loss realization uses maintained auxiliary state.
statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\), the selected block is updated by \[x_{i(k)}^{k+1}=x_{i(k)}^k-\alpha\nabla_{i(k)}f(x^k).\] The extract states that this iteration converges if a minimizer exists, \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth, and \(0<\alpha<2/L\). For \(f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^r\ell_j(a_j^\top x-b_j)\), maintaining the linear-predictor vector \(y^k=Ax^k\) permits the selected-block update and the incremental state update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+A_{:,i(k)}(x_{i(k)}^{k+1}-x_{i(k)}^k).\] If each scalar derivative \(\ell_j'\) has \(O(1)\) evaluation cost, the stated iteration cost is \(O(rn_{i(k)})\).
statement_plain: Randomized block-coordinate gradient descent updates only the selected block. The extract states convergence for an existing minimizer, an L-smooth objective, and a stepsize strictly between zero and 2/L, without specifying the sampling law or convergence mode. For sums of scalar losses of linear predictors, maintaining Ax gives an extended coordinate-friendly implementation with the stated cost O(r times the selected block dimension).
statement_title: Randomized block-coordinate gradient descent with maintained linear-predictor state

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim\text{ is a Riemannian quotient manifold}\)
conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \frac{\mathrm D}{\mathrm dt}Z=\mathrm D\pi(\bar c)\left[\frac{\overline{\mathrm D}}{\mathrm dt}\bar Z\right]\)
scope_note: Represents covariant differentiation along a quotient-manifold curve through total-space differentiation of a horizontal lift.
statement_latex: Let \(\bar c:I\to\overline{\mathcal M}\) be a horizontal curve, let \(c=\pi\circ\bar c\) be the corresponding smooth curve on the Riemannian quotient manifold \(\mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim\), and let \(Z\in\mathfrak X(c)\) have horizontal lift \(\bar Z=\operatorname{lift}(Z)\). Then \[\frac{\mathrm D}{\mathrm dt}Z=\mathrm D\pi(\bar c)\left[\frac{\overline{\mathrm D}}{\mathrm dt}\bar Z\right].\]
statement_plain: Along a horizontal representative of a curve on a Riemannian quotient manifold, the covariant derivative of a vector field is the quotient differential applied to the total-space covariant derivative of its horizontal lift.
statement_title: Covariant Derivative Through a Horizontal Lift

assumptions_latex: g(t)\text{ solves the preceding Cauchy problem for }t\in[t_0,\infty)
conclusion_latex: \forall t\in[t_0,\infty),\quad (M,g(t))\text{ is a complete Riemannian manifold}
scope_note: “The preceding Cauchy problem” refers to the adjacent tensor-valued metric evolution; its full hypotheses are not repeated in this corollary extract.
statement_latex: Let \((M,g_0)\) be a complete Riemannian manifold. If \(g(t)\), \(t\in[t_0,\infty)\), is a solution of the preceding Cauchy problem, then \((M,g(t))\) is a complete Riemannian manifold for every \(t\in[t_0,\infty)\).
statement_plain: If the reference Riemannian manifold is complete, every metric produced by the preceding Cauchy problem is complete throughout the stated forward-time interval.
statement_title: Completeness Preservation under the Preceding Metric Evolution

conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is closed in }\overline{\mathcal M}\text{ and embedded},\quad \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}-\dim\mathcal N,\quad \mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x)\quad\forall x\in\mathcal M.
scope_note: Gives closedness, embeddedness, dimension, and tangent spaces for a nonempty level set whose defining map is surjective along the level set.
statement_latex: Let h:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal N be smooth, let \alpha\in\mathcal N, and suppose \varnothing\neq\mathcal M=h^{-1}(\alpha). If \operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=\dim\mathcal N for every x\in\mathcal M, then \mathcal M is closed in \overline{\mathcal M}, is an embedded submanifold of \overline{\mathcal M} with \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}-\dim\mathcal N, and satisfies \mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x) for every x\in\mathcal M.
statement_plain: A nonempty level set on which the defining map has full rank is closed and is an embedded submanifold. Its codimension is the target manifold's dimension, and its tangent space is the kernel of the differential.
statement_title: Regular Level-Set Submanifold Theorem

conclusion_latex: \dim T_xM=n,\quad \text{and a scalar product on }T_xM\text{ is a Riemannian metric on }T_xM.
scope_note: Pointwise inner-product structure on a differentiable manifold.
statement_latex: Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional differentiable manifold and $x\in M$. The tangent space $T_xM$ is a real vector space of dimension $n$. A scalar product on $T_xM$ is called a Riemannian metric on $T_xM$.
statement_plain: For an n-dimensional differentiable manifold, each tangent space is an n-dimensional real vector space, and a scalar product on that tangent space is called a Riemannian metric there.
statement_title: Riemannian Metric on a Tangent Space

assumptions_latex: \mathrm{GL}_p\text{ acts freely on }\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}\text{ by }X\mapsto XA
\mathbb{RP}^{k}\text{ denotes the space of lines in }\mathbb{R}^{k+1}
conclusion_latex: \mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}/\mathrm{GL}_p\cong\operatorname{Grass}(p,n),\qquad \dim\operatorname{Grass}(p,n)=p(n-p),\qquad \operatorname{Grass}(1,n)\cong\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}.
scope_note: Defines the real Grassmann manifold through full-rank matrix representatives and records its dimension. The extract's notation \(\operatorname{Grass}(1,n)=\mathbb{RP}^{n}\) conflicts with the standard convention, under which the space of lines in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is \(\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}\).
statement_latex:
For integers $1\le p\le n$, let $\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}$ be the set of full-column-rank real $n\times p$ matrices. The quotient under the right action $X\mapsto XA$ of $\mathrm{GL}_p$ is the Grassmann manifold of $p$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$:
\[
\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}/\mathrm{GL}_p\cong\operatorname{Grass}(p,n),\qquad \dim\operatorname{Grass}(p,n)=p(n-p).
\]
Consequently, with the standard indexing of real projective space, $\operatorname{Grass}(1,n)\cong\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$; the extract prints $\mathbb{RP}^{n}$.
statement_plain: For 1 ≤ p ≤ n, quotienting the full-column-rank n-by-p real matrices by invertible changes of basis gives the Grassmann manifold of p-dimensional subspaces of R^n. Its dimension is p(n−p). Under standard projective-space indexing, Grass(1,n) is RP^(n−1); the extract instead prints RP^n.
statement_title: Grassmann Manifold as a Quotient

scope_note: Definition and elementary properties of real square orthogonal matrices.
statement_latex: A matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is orthogonal if $P^{T}P=PP^{T}=I$. Then $P^{-1}=P^{T}$, $|\det P|=1$, and the rows and columns of $P$ are orthonormal. For every $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$, $\|Px\|_{2}=\|x\|_{2}$ and $(Px)^{T}(Py)=x^{T}y$, so orthogonality is preserved under the transformation $x\mapsto Px$.
statement_plain: A real square matrix is orthogonal when its transpose is its inverse. Its rows and columns are orthonormal, its determinant has absolute value one, and it preserves Euclidean norms, inner products, and orthogonality.
statement_title: Orthogonal matrices and preservation of Euclidean geometry

assumptions_latex: R\text{ is a retraction on }\mathcal M
conclusion_latex: f(x)-f\bigl(R_x(-\alpha\operatorname{grad}f(x))\bigr)\ge r\alpha\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|^2\quad\text{upon termination}
scope_note: Geometric backtracking along the negative Riemannian gradient using a retraction and sufficient-decrease acceptance.
statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathcal M\), \(\bar\alpha>0\), a retraction \(R\), and \(\tau,r\in(0,1)\), initialize \(\alpha=\bar\alpha\). While \[f(x)-f\bigl(R_x(-\alpha\operatorname{grad}f(x))\bigr)<r\alpha\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|^2,\] set \(\alpha\leftarrow\tau\alpha\). Return \(\alpha\).
statement_plain: Starting from the prescribed trial step, repeatedly contract it by tau while the retracted negative-gradient step fails the Armijo sufficient-decrease test, and return the accepted step size.
statement_title: Riemannian Armijo Backtracking Step Search

assumptions_latex: \exp_{x_i}(tX_i)\text{ and }f(\exp_{x_i}(tX_i))\text{ are defined for each tested }t
conclusion_latex: t_i=t\text{ is accepted if }f(\exp_{x_i}(tX_i))-f(x_i)\leq\varepsilon t\,df_{x_i}(X_i),\text{ beginning with }t=1\text{ and reducing }t\text{ otherwise; no finite-acceptance conclusion is asserted}.
scope_note: Exponential-map backtracking for the exact Newton direction. The extract specifies neither a reduction factor nor assumptions guaranteeing finite acceptance.
statement_latex: At iterate $x_i$, let $X_i=-(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_i))^{-1}df_{x_i}$ be the exact Riemannian Newton direction and choose $0<\varepsilon<\tfrac12$. Initialize $t=1$ and form $x=\exp_{x_i}(tX_i)$. If $f(x)-f(x_i)\leq \varepsilon t\,df_{x_i}(X_i)$, accept $t_i=t$; otherwise reduce $t$ and repeat the test. The extract does not provide conditions ensuring that the test is eventually satisfied.
statement_plain: Start with a unit step along the exact Riemannian Newton direction. Accept it if the exponential-map trial point satisfies the stated Armijo inequality; otherwise reduce the step and retest. No reduction schedule or finite-termination guarantee is supplied.
statement_title: Armijo Backtracking for an Exact Riemannian Newton Direction

assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a symmetric covariant tensor field}
F_i\text{ satisfies the same bounds at }x_i
conclusion_latex: df(x_i)[-F_i^{-1}df(x_i)]\le -m_1\|df(x_i)\|^2\le0,\qquad x_{i+1}=\exp_{x_i}(-t_iF_i^{-1}df(x_i))
scope_note: Defines tensor-scaled descent directions and the inverse-tensor exponential-map iteration; the separate cross-referenced transfer theorem is not folded into this algorithm statement.
statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a symmetric covariant tensor field satisfying \[r_1\|X\|^2\le F(X,X)\le r_2\|X\|^2,\qquad 0<r_1\le r_2,\] for all tangent vectors \(X\). Then the induced map \(F^\flat:TM\to T^*M\) is invertible, and its inverse satisfies \[m_1\|\omega\|^2\le F^{-1}(\omega,\omega)\le m_2\|\omega\|^2,\qquad m_1=\frac{r_1}{r_2^2},\quad m_2=\frac1{r_1}.\] If \(df(x)\ne0\), then \(-F^{-1}df(x)\) is a strict descent direction because \[df(x)[-F^{-1}df(x)]=-F^{-1}(df(x),df(x))\le -m_1\|df(x)\|^2<0.\] Thus, for tensors \(F_i\) satisfying the same bounds, one may iterate \[x_{i+1}=\exp_{x_i}\!\left(-t_iF_i^{-1}df(x_i)\right),\qquad t_i>0.\]
statement_plain: A uniformly positive-definite symmetric tensor has an inverse that maps the differential to a strict descent direction. The resulting preconditioned Riemannian gradient method takes a positive step along that direction using the exponential map.
statement_title: Uniformly positive-definite tensor-scaled Riemannian gradient iteration

assumptions_latex: H_k\text{ defines the quadratic trust-region model on }T_{x_k}\mathcal M
conclusion_latex: \eta_k\text{ is returned at a negative-curvature, trust-region-boundary, or prescribed stopping event}
scope_note: Tangent-space truncated conjugate-gradient procedure with negative-curvature, boundary, and stopping exits.
statement_latex: Initialize \(\eta^0=0\), \(r_0=\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\), and \(\delta_0=-r_0\). At iteration \(j\), if \(\langle\delta_j,H_k\delta_j\rangle_{x_k}\leq0\), return the model-minimizing point on \(\eta^j+\tau\delta_j\) lying on \(\|\eta\|=\Delta_k\). Otherwise set \[\alpha_j=\frac{\langle r_j,r_j\rangle_{x_k}}{\langle\delta_j,H_k\delta_j\rangle_{x_k}},\qquad \eta^{j+1}=\eta^j+\alpha_j\delta_j.\] If \(\|\eta^{j+1}\|\geq\Delta_k\), return the intersection of \(\eta^j+\tau\delta_j\) with the trust-region boundary. If the stopping criterion holds, return \(\eta^{j+1}\). Otherwise set \[r_{j+1}=r_j+\alpha_jH_k\delta_j,\quad \beta_{j+1}=\frac{\langle r_{j+1},r_{j+1}\rangle_{x_k}}{\langle r_j,r_j\rangle_{x_k}},\quad \delta_{j+1}=-r_{j+1}+\beta_{j+1}\delta_j,\] and continue.
statement_plain: Starting from the zero tangent step and negative gradient direction, truncated CG returns a trust-region boundary point upon nonpositive curvature or boundary crossing, returns the current CG iterate when its stopping test holds, and otherwise continues with the standard residual and conjugate-direction recurrences.
statement_title: Riemannian Truncated-CG Trust-Region Solver

assumptions_latex: \{k_i\}\text{ is a subsequence of the derivative-free trust-region iterates.}
conclusion_latex: \lim_{i\to+\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_{k_i})\rVert=0
scope_note: Subsequence consistency between model-gradient and true-gradient criticality in the derivative-free trust-region method.
statement_latex: For every subsequence \(\{k_i\}\), if \(\lim_{i\to+\infty}\lVert g_{k_i}\rVert=0\), then \(\lim_{i\to+\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_{k_i})\rVert=0\).
statement_plain: Along any subsequence where the model-gradient norm tends to zero, the true-gradient norm also tends to zero.
statement_title: Transfer from Vanishing Model Gradients to True Gradients

assumptions_latex: v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)\text{ is a quadratic polynomial of degree at most }d
conclusion_latex: \exists\,\sigma_\infty>0\text{ independent of }v\text{ such that }\max_{x\in B(0;1)}|v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)|\geq\sigma_\infty;\quad d=1\Rightarrow\sigma_\infty\geq1,\quad d=2\Rightarrow\sigma_\infty\geq\tfrac14.
scope_note: A coefficient-to-function norm bound for natural-basis polynomial models used in derivative-free interpolation geometry.
statement_latex:
Let \(v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)\) be a quadratic polynomial of degree at most \(d\), where \(\bar\phi\) is the natural basis and \(\|v\|_\infty=1\). Then there exists a constant \(\sigma_\infty>0\), independent of \(v\), such that
\[
\max_{x\in B(0;1)}\left|v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)\right|\geq \sigma_\infty.
\]
Moreover, \(\sigma_\infty\geq1\) for \(d=1\), and \(\sigma_\infty\geq\tfrac14\) for \(d=2\).
statement_plain: For a natural-basis quadratic polynomial of degree at most d whose coefficient vector has infinity norm one, the maximum absolute value on the unit ball is uniformly bounded below by a positive constant independent of the coefficient vector. The stated lower bounds are 1 for degree one and 1/4 for degree two.
statement_title: Uniform Supremum Lower Bound for Normalized Natural-Basis Polynomials

assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}\text{ is the sequence of iterates produced by GPS}
conclusion_latex: \exists K,\widehat{x}\quad \{x^k\}_{k\in K}\text{ is a refining subsequence and }\widehat{x}\text{ is its corresponding refined point}
scope_note: Existence of a refining subsequence and corresponding refined point for generalized pattern search.
statement_latex: Let \(\{x^k\}\) be the iterates produced by GPS applied to \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) with bounded level sets. Then there exist a refining subsequence \(\{x^k\}_{k\in K}\) and a corresponding refined point \(\widehat{x}\).
statement_plain: For GPS applied to a function with bounded level sets, a refining subsequence and its corresponding refined point exist.
statement_title: Existence of a GPS Refined Point

conclusion_latex: \text{Nelder--Mead uses an }n\text{-dimensional simplex as its search geometry.}
scope_note: Defines the geometric object used by Nelder–Mead and states its role in the search.
statement_latex: The Nelder\text{--}Mead method searches for a minimum by traversing the search space with a simplex. An \(n\)-dimensional simplex is the simplest polytope in dimension \(n\); in one dimension it is a line segment, and in two dimensions it is a triangle.
statement_plain: The Nelder–Mead method searches for a minimum by moving a simplex through the search space. An n-dimensional simplex is the simplest polytope in dimension n; in one dimension it is a line segment, and in two dimensions it is a triangle.
statement_title: Simplex search geometry of the Nelder–Mead method

conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathbb R^n\;\forall\bar\Delta>0\;\exists\{\widetilde f_\Delta\}_{\Delta\in(0,\bar\Delta]}\text{ fully linear at }x;\quad \text{fixed constants mean }\exists\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\;\forall x:\ \kappa_f(x)=\kappa_f,\ \kappa_g(x)=\kappa_g
scope_note: Extends the pointwise definition to every center and maximum radius and distinguishes center-dependent from center-independent accuracy constants.
statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathcal C^1\). Models \(\widetilde f_\Delta\) are fully linear models of \(f\) if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and every \(\bar\Delta>0\), there exists a class \(\{\widetilde f_\Delta\}_{\Delta\in(0,\bar\Delta]}\) of fully linear models of \(f\) at \(x\). They are fully linear with constants \(\kappa_f\) and \(\kappa_g\) if, for every such \(x\) and \(\bar\Delta\), the class can be chosen with the constants in the pointwise definition satisfying \(\kappa_f(x)=\kappa_f\) and \(\kappa_g(x)=\kappa_g\), independently of \(x\).
statement_plain: Models are fully linear for a continuously differentiable function when a fully linear radius-parameterized class exists at every center and for every positive maximum radius. They have fixed constants when the function-value and gradient accuracy constants can be chosen independently of the center.
statement_title: Fully Linear Models and Center-Independent Constants

conclusion_latex: \overline{\{v/\lVert v\rVert:v\in V\}}=S^{n-1}
scope_note: Definition for a set of nonzero directions in Euclidean space.
statement_latex: A set \(V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) is asymptotically dense if \(\{v/\lVert v\rVert:v\in V\}\) is dense in the unit sphere \(S^{n-1}=\{w\in\mathbb{R}^n:\lVert w\rVert=1\}\).
statement_plain: A set of nonzero directions is asymptotically dense when its normalized directions are dense on the unit sphere.
statement_title: Asymptotically Dense Direction Set

assumptions_latex: X_*\text{ is a finite list of prediction inputs}
conclusion_latex: \mu_*=m(X_*)+K(X_*,X)\bigl(K(X,X)+vI\bigr)^{-1}\bigl(y-m(X)\bigr),\qquad v_*=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(K(X_*,X_*)-K(X_*,X)\bigl(K(X,X)+vI\bigr)^{-1}K(X,X_*)\right)+\varepsilon.
scope_note: Posterior mean and marginal latent-function variance at finitely many prediction points using a scalar observation-noise variance.
statement_latex: Given a Gaussian process with mean function $m$, covariance kernel $k$, training inputs $X$, observations $y$, and scalar observation-noise variance $v$, let $X_*$ denote the prediction inputs and suppose $K(X,X)+vI$ is invertible. Define $T=K(X_*,X)\bigl(K(X,X)+vI\bigr)^{-1}$. Compute $\mu_*=m(X_*)+T\bigl(y-m(X)\bigr)$ and $S_*=K(X_*,X_*)-TK(X,X_*)$. Return $\mu_*$ and $v_*=\operatorname{diag}(S_*)+\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon$ is a machine-scale numerical offset.
statement_plain: Form the cross-covariance times the inverse of the noise-adjusted training covariance. Use it to compute the posterior mean and covariance at the requested points, then return the covariance diagonal with a machine-scale offset as the marginal latent-function variances.
statement_title: Gaussian-process prediction with homoscedastic observation noise

conclusion_latex: \text{If the procedure terminates, }f(x)\ge f(x')\text{ and it returns the final selected }x;\text{ no local-minimum or monotonic-return guarantee follows.}
scope_note: Literal extracted update and return behavior; the final nonimproving neighbor is returned, so the procedure can return a point worse than its predecessor and does not by itself certify a local minimum.
statement_latex: Repeat \(x'\leftarrow x\) and choose \(x\in\arg\min_{y\in N(x')}f(y)\) until \(f(x)\ge f(x')\); then return the final selected \(x\).
statement_plain: Replace the current point by a best neighbor at each iteration. Stop when that selected neighbor is not strictly better than its predecessor and, literally as extracted, return the selected neighbor rather than restoring the predecessor.
statement_title: Best-improvement neighborhood heuristic

assumptions_latex: A specified interpolation, regression, or other model-construction theorem supplies sufficient accuracy conditions.
The smoothness, data-locality, geometry, and model-class hypotheses required by that theorem are declared.
conclusion_latex: Every model released for an ordinary trial is valid under its declared accuracy theorem on the active trust region.
scope_note: Reuse, revalidation, and rebuilding of a derivative-free model as the active center, radius, or sample set changes.
statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), associate \(m_k\) with a declared model class, center \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k\), data set \(Y_k\), and a construction theorem whose hypotheses imply the required fully linear or fully quadratic bounds on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\). The manager may release \(m_k\) for a trial only while those hypotheses remain valid at that exact center and scale. After any change of center, radius, data, or model coefficients, it must revalidate the theorem's hypotheses; if they fail, it requests the separately specified geometry or sampling repair and rebuilds the model before releasing another ordinary trial.
statement_plain: A trust-region model may be reused only while its declared construction theorem still guarantees the required accuracy at the current center and radius; otherwise it must be repaired or rebuilt.
statement_title: Scale-Valid Trust-Region Model Lifecycle

assumptions_latex: \{\bar\phi_0,�ldots,\bar\phi_p\}\text{ is the chosen initial polynomial basis}
conclusion_latex: \text{Either a zero pivot detects nonpoisedness, or the completed basis satisfies }\ell_j(y^i)=\delta_{ij}.
scope_note: Construction of the Lagrange basis for a prescribed interpolation set, including detection of nonpoisedness through a zero pivot.
statement_latex: Initialize \(\ell_i=\bar\phi_i\) for \(i=0,\ldots,p\). For each \(i\), choose \(j_i\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\le j\le p}|\ell_i(y^j)|\). If \(\ell_i(y^{j_i})=0\), stop: \(Y\) is not poised. Otherwise exchange \(y^i\) and \(y^{j_i}\), set \(\ell_i\leftarrow\ell_i/\ell_i(y^i)\), and, for every \(j\ne i\), set \(\ell_j\leftarrow\ell_j-\ell_j(y^i)\ell_i\).
statement_plain: Starting from a polynomial basis, pivot successively on the remaining sample point where the current polynomial has largest absolute value. A zero pivot detects that the set is not poised; otherwise the algorithm swaps, normalizes, and eliminates to construct the Lagrange basis.
statement_title: Pivoted construction of Lagrange polynomials

conclusion_latex: \|\widehat{\mathbf x}_i(\mathbf z)-\widehat{\mathbf x}_i(\mathbf z')\|\le \widehat L_i\|\mathbf z-\mathbf z'\|\quad\forall\mathbf z,\mathbf z'\in X,\qquad \operatorname{Fix}(\widehat{\mathbf x}_i)=\operatorname{Stat}(\mathrm{Problem}\ (3.167))\ne\varnothing
scope_note: Properties of each agent-indexed best-response map under the unexpanded setting of Theorem 4.16.
statement_latex: In the setting of Theorem 4.16, for every \(i=1,\ldots,I\), the map \(\mathbf z\mapsto\widehat{\mathbf x}_i(\mathbf z)\), defined on \(X\), is \(\widehat L_i\)-Lipschitz continuous on \(X\). Its fixed-point set coincides with the stationary-solution set of Problem (3.167), and hence it has a fixed point.
statement_plain: Under the referenced theorem's setting, each agent-indexed best-response map is Lipschitz continuous. Its fixed points are exactly the stationary solutions of the referenced problem, so at least one fixed point exists.
statement_title: Lipschitz continuity and fixed points of the distributed SCA best-response map

assumptions_latex: x(k)\text{ is produced by the specified gossip algorithm}
0<\lambda_g<1\text{ is the second-largest eigenvalue of }\bar W_g
conclusion_latex: \forall k\ge0:\quad \mathbb E\!\left[\left\|x(k)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m x_j(0)\mathbf1\right\|^2\right]\le\lambda_g^k\left\|x(0)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m x_j(0)\mathbf1\right\|^2
scope_note: Guarantee for the specified gossip algorithm on a connected graph.
statement_latex: Assume that \(G\) is connected and that \(x(k)\) is produced by the gossip algorithm. Let \(\bar W_g=\mathbb E[W_g(k)]\), and let \(0<\lambda_g<1\) be its second-largest eigenvalue. Then, for every \(k\ge0\), \[\mathbb E\!\left[\left\|x(k)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m x_j(0)\mathbf1\right\|^2\right]\le \lambda_g^k\left\|x(0)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m x_j(0)\mathbf1\right\|^2.\]
statement_plain: On a connected graph, the specified gossip iterates approach the initial-state average in mean square, with the stated geometric contraction factor.
statement_title: Mean-square geometric contraction of pairwise gossip consensus

assumptions_latex: \text{the assumptions under which the MSD expressions (5.65) and (5.79) hold}
conclusion_latex: \mathrm{MSD}_{\mathrm{cent}}<\mathrm{MSD}_{\mathrm{ncop,av}}.
scope_note: Small-step-size performance comparison between centralized aggregation and average noncooperative learning.
statement_latex: Under the assumptions yielding the centralized and average noncooperative MSD expressions (5.65) and (5.79), respectively, and for sufficiently small step sizes, \mathrm{MSD}_{\mathrm{cent}}<\mathrm{MSD}_{\mathrm{ncop,av}}.
statement_plain: For sufficiently small step sizes, centralized aggregation has strictly smaller mean-square deviation than the average noncooperative architecture under the model assumptions used to derive the two MSD expressions.
statement_title: Centralized MSD Is Smaller Than Average Noncooperative MSD

assumptions_latex: \{\mathbf x^k\},\{\mathbf y^k\},\{\boldsymbol\phi^k\}\text{ are generated by Algorithm 10.}
conclusion_latex: \phi_{lb}\mathbf 1\le\boldsymbol\phi^k\le\phi_{ub}\mathbf 1\quad\forall k\in\mathbb N_+,\qquad \sup_{k\in\mathbb N_+}\|\mathbf y_{(i)}^k-\bar{\mathbf y}_{\phi}^k\|<\infty,\quad \sup_{k\in\mathbb N_+}\|\mathbf x_{(i)}^k-\widetilde{\mathbf x}_i^k\|<\infty\quad\forall i
scope_note: Boundedness of the weights, tracking disagreement, and local update displacement generated by Algorithm 10.
statement_latex: Let \(\{\mathbf x^k\}\), \(\{\mathbf y^k\}\), and \(\{\boldsymbol\phi^k\}\) be generated by Algorithm 10 in the setting of Theorem 4.16 under Assumptions 4.18--4.19. Then finite constants \(\phi_{lb},\phi_{ub}>0\) satisfy \(\phi_{lb}\mathbf 1\le\boldsymbol\phi^k\le\phi_{ub}\mathbf 1\) for every \(k\in\mathbb N_+\). Moreover, for every \(i=1,\ldots,I\), \[\sup_{k\in\mathbb N_+}\|\mathbf y_{(i)}^k-\bar{\mathbf y}_{\phi}^k\|<\infty,\qquad \sup_{k\in\mathbb N_+}\|\mathbf x_{(i)}^k-\widetilde{\mathbf x}_i^k\|<\infty.\]
statement_plain: Under the stated algorithmic assumptions, the weight vector remains uniformly bounded above and away from zero. Each agent's tracking disagreement and local update displacement are also uniformly bounded.
statement_title: Uniform boundedness of distributed SCA auxiliary sequences

assumptions_latex: W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ is a decentralized mixing matrix}
conclusion_latex: \mathbf{x}^k\to\mathbf1\bar x\ \text{for every }\mathbf{x}^0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad W\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ \mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top,\ 1=|\lambda_1|>|\lambda_2|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n|.
scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for convergence to the arithmetic average from every initialization.
statement_latex: Let $x_i\in\mathbb R^p$, let $\mathbf{x}^0=\operatorname{stack}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, and consider $\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W\mathbf{x}^k$, where $W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ is a decentralized mixing matrix. If the eigenvalues are ordered so that $|\lambda_1|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n|$, then the iteration converges for every $\mathbf{x}^0$ to consensus at $\bar x=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$ if and only if $W\mathbf1=\mathbf1$, $\mathbf1^\top W=\mathbf1^\top$, and $1=|\lambda_1|>|\lambda_2|\ge\cdots\ge|\lambda_n|$.
statement_plain: Linear decentralized averaging converges from every initial state to the arithmetic average exactly when the mixing matrix fixes consensus vectors, preserves the mean, and has every nonconsensus eigenvalue strictly inside the unit circle.
statement_title: Convergence characterization for linear decentralized averaging

conclusion_latex: \min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)\mid x_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=b\right\}=\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+I_{\mathcal C}(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\right).
scope_note: Defines allocation of a vector resource among activities under componentwise nonnegativity and a fixed aggregate budget.
statement_latex:
For variables \(x_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(i=1,\ldots,N\), the allocation problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
x_i\geq 0\ \ (i=1,\ldots,N),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=b.
\]
Defining
\[
\mathcal C=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\mid x_i\geq0\ \text{for all }i,\ \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=b\right\},
\]
the same problem has the extended-valued representation
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+I_{\mathcal C}(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\right).
\]
statement_plain: Allocate a vector resource among N activities to minimize the sum of their individual costs. Every allocation is componentwise nonnegative, and the allocations sum to the available resource vector b. Equivalently, add the indicator function of this allocation set to the separable objective.
statement_title: Separable Resource-Allocation Model and Indicator Representation

assumptions_latex: h_1,\ldots,h_n\text{ satisfy the standing convexity assumptions and are }L\text{-smooth}
W\text{ is a decentralized mixing matrix for the decentralization claim}
conclusion_latex: \mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W\mathbf{x}^{k}-\alpha\nabla h(\mathbf{x}^{k}),\qquad \mathbf{x}^{k}\to\mathbf{x}^{\star}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf{x}}\left(h(\mathbf{x})+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}\right).
scope_note: Combine-then-adapt DGD, including its decentralized implementation and its fixed-stepsize convergence boundary: the stated guarantee concerns the quadratic-penalty problem rather than the original exact-consensus problem.
statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}} h(\mathbf{x})+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}\), where \(\|\mathbf{x}\|_{I-W}^{2}=0\) if and only if \(\mathbf{x}\) is in consensus. Gradient descent with stepsize \(\alpha\) yields decentralized gradient descent (combine-then-adapt): \(\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=W\mathbf{x}^{k}-\alpha\nabla h(\mathbf{x}^{k})\). If the penalty problem has a solution, the local functions satisfy the source's standing convexity assumptions and are \(L\)-smooth, and \(0<\alpha<(1+\lambda_n(W))/L\), then \(\mathbf{x}^{k}\) converges to a solution of the penalty problem. When \(W\) is a decentralized mixing matrix, multiplication by \(W\) uses neighbor communication and all remaining operations are local. For fixed \(\alpha\), this is not an asserted convergence guarantee for the exact-consensus problem; small \(\alpha\) only motivates the penalty approximation.
statement_plain: Gradient descent on the quadratic consensus-penalty formulation produces DGD, also called combine-then-adapt: mix with W and subtract the local gradient step. Under the stated smoothness, solvability, and stepsize assumptions, the iterates converge to a solution of the penalty problem. A decentralized mixing matrix permits neighbor-only communication. The extract does not claim exact convergence to the original consensus problem for a fixed positive stepsize.
statement_title: Decentralized Gradient Descent as Consensus-Penalty Gradient Descent

assumptions_latex: \text{The center increments the sequence number for each new value of }V
|A|\text{ is the number of bidirectional network links}
\text{Endpoints exchange stored values and sequence numbers when a failed link recovers}
conclusion_latex: \text{messages per new value of }V<2|A|,\qquad\text{order-preserving link delivery is unnecessary}.
scope_note: Center-originated flooding with stale-message suppression, recovery exchange, and a transmission-count bound.
statement_latex: After each change of the center value V, the center sends the new value with an incremented sequence number to all its neighbors. A processor accepts and forwards a received value to neighbors other than its sender only if its sequence number exceeds the locally stored number; otherwise it discards the message. When a failed link becomes operational, its endpoints exchange their stored values and sequence numbers. If |A| is the number of bidirectional network links, the scheme uses fewer than 2|A| messages per new value and does not require links to preserve transmission order.
statement_plain: The center floods each new value with a larger sequence number. Nodes forward only messages newer than their stored version, and endpoints exchange stored versions when a link recovers. An update uses fewer than twice the number of bidirectional links in messages, and FIFO delivery is unnecessary.
statement_title: Sequence-Numbered Flooding Broadcast

assumptions_latex: \mathbf x_{(i)}^0\in X,\quad \phi_{(i)}^0=1,\quad \mathbf y_{(i)}^0=\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^0),\quad i=1,\ldots,I
conclusion_latex: (\phi_{(i)}^{k+1},\mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1},\mathbf y_{(i)}^{k+1})\text{ are generated by the stated local-SCA, push-sum, and gradient-tracking recursions.}
scope_note: Local surrogate minimization followed by push-sum averaging and gradient tracking.
statement_latex:
Initialize \(\mathbf x_{(i)}^0\in X\), \(\phi_{(i)}^0=1\), and \(\mathbf y_{(i)}^0=\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^0)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,I\), with \(\gamma^k\in(0,1]\). At iteration \(k\), each agent computes
\[\widetilde{\mathbf x}_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x_{(i)}\in X}\left\{\widetilde f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}\mid\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)+\bigl(I\mathbf y_{(i)}^k-\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)\bigr)^T(\mathbf x_{(i)}-\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)+G(\mathbf x_{(i)})\right\},\]
\[\mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1/2}=\mathbf x_{(i)}^k+\gamma^k(\widetilde{\mathbf x}_i^k-\mathbf x_{(i)}^k).\]
After exchanging variables with its in-neighbors, it updates
\[\phi_{(i)}^{k+1}=\sum_{j=1}^I a_{ij}^k\phi_{(j)}^k,\qquad \mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1}=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^I a_{ij}^k\phi_{(j)}^k\mathbf x_{(j)}^{k+1/2}}{\phi_{(i)}^{k+1}},\]
\[\mathbf y_{(i)}^{k+1}=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^I a_{ij}^k\phi_{(j)}^k\mathbf y_{(j)}^k+\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^{k+1})-\nabla f_i(\mathbf x_{(i)}^k)}{\phi_{(i)}^{k+1}}.\]
The iterations continue until the termination criterion is met.
statement_plain: SONATA alternates an agent-local surrogate minimization and relaxed update with push-sum averaging and gradient tracking over the current directed communication graph.
statement_title: SONATA distributed SCA iteration over time-varying digraphs

assumptions_latex: A deterministic tie-breaking order is fixed.
conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Krum}_f(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=v_{i^*}\), where \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{i}s_i\).
scope_note: Original one-vector Krum rule with squared Euclidean distance scores.
statement_latex: Input \(n\) vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), a Byzantine upper bound \(f\), and a fixed tie-breaking order, with \(n\ge2f+3\). No iterative state is initialized. For each \(i\), let \(N_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\) contain the \(n-f-2\) indices having smallest squared distances \(\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert_2^2\), resolving ties by the fixed order, and compute \(s_i=\sum_{j\in N_i}\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert_2^2\). Choose \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i s_i\) using the same order, stop, and output \(v_{i^*}\).
statement_plain: Krum scores each reported update by its squared distances to its nearest prescribed neighbors and outputs the single update with minimum score.
statement_title: Krum aggregation

conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}x_i^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f_i}\left(x_i^k-(z^k)_i-(u^k)_i\right),\\ z^{k+1}&=\Pi_{\mathcal C}(x^{k+1}+u^k),\\ u_i^{k+1}&=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-(z^{k+1})_i,\end{aligned}\qquad \Pi_{\mathcal C}\text{ separates into }n\text{ fixed-sum simplex projections in }\mathbb R^N.
scope_note: Gives an allocation-specific proximal iteration whose coupling step projects onto the nonnegative fixed-budget allocation set.
statement_latex:
Let
\[
\mathcal C=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\mid x_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=b\right\}.
\]
The iteration is
\[
x_i^{k+1}:=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f_i}\!\left(x_i^k-(z^k)_i-(u^k)_i\right),\qquad i=1,\ldots,N,
\]
\[
z^{k+1}:=\Pi_{\mathcal C}(x^{k+1}+u^k),
\]
\[
u_i^{k+1}:=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-(z^{k+1})_i,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,N.
\]
Projection onto \(\mathcal C\) separates by resource coordinate into \(n\) independent projections in \(\mathbb R^N\) onto nonnegative simplices having the corresponding fixed sums \(b_j\).
statement_plain: Update each activity block using its local proximal map, project the assembled vector onto the nonnegative fixed-budget allocation set, and update the auxiliary block by the discrepancy between the local and projected allocations. The allocation-set projection decomposes across resource coordinates into n independent fixed-sum simplex projections in R^N.
statement_title: Proximal Splitting Iteration for Resource Allocation

assumptions_latex: f_i:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is closed, convex, and proper for every }i
\text{For the convergence conclusion, the hypotheses of the applicable ADMM convergence theorem hold}
conclusion_latex: x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{Prox}_{(1/\alpha)f_i}\!\left(\bar x^k-\frac1\alpha u_i^k\right),\qquad u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+\alpha\left(x_i^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1}\right),\quad\text{after the dual variables have zero mean; convergence then follows conditionally from ADMM, and the stated DRS iteration is equivalent.}
scope_note: Parameter-server ADMM for a sum of closed proper convex functions represented using replicated variables constrained to consensus.
statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^p}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), introduce replicated variables satisfying \(x_i=y\). With \(\alpha>0\), ADMM yields local primal updates, a centralized averaging update, and dual updates. Once the dual variables have zero mean, the iteration simplifies to \(x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{Prox}_{(1/\alpha)f_i}(\bar x^k-(1/\alpha)u_i^k)\) and \(u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+\alpha(x_i^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1})\). Its convergence is inherited from ADMM whenever the applicable ADMM convergence hypotheses hold. Equivalently, DRS applied to \(\delta_C(x_1,\ldots,x_n)+\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) gives \(x_i^{k+1/2}=\operatorname{Prox}_{(1/\alpha)f_i}(z_i^k)\) and \(z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k-\bar z^k+2\bar x^{k+1/2}-x_i^{k+1/2}\).
statement_plain: Replicate the common decision and enforce equality with a central consensus variable. Agents perform local proximal and dual updates, while a central reduction computes the average. After the dual variables acquire zero mean, the displayed simplified iteration applies. Its convergence is conditional on the hypotheses of the underlying ADMM convergence result. Douglas–Rachford splitting of the consensus-indicator formulation gives an equivalent iteration.
statement_title: Centralized consensus ADMM and equivalent DRS iteration

conclusion_latex: \{x_k\}\text{ is a minimizing sequence; if }\sup_{k\in K}t_k<+\infty\text{ and }\operatorname*{argmin}(3.0.1)\ne\varnothing,\text{ then }x_k\to x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}(3.0.1).
scope_note: Extraction-grounded convergence theorem for the primal penalty bundle method when infinitely many descent steps occur.
statement_latex: Apply Algorithm 3.1.4 to problem \((3.0.1)\) with stopping tolerance \(\underline\delta=0\), and let \(K\) be its infinite set of descent-step indices. If \[\sum_{k\in K}t_k=+\infty,\] then \(\{x_k\}\) is a minimizing sequence. If, additionally, \(\sup_{k\in K}t_k<+\infty\) and the problem has a nonempty solution set, then the entire sequence \(\{x_k\}\) converges to a solution.
statement_plain: With zero stopping tolerance and infinitely many descent steps, divergence of the sum of their parameters makes the iterates a minimizing sequence. If those parameters are also bounded above and a minimizer exists, the whole sequence converges to a minimizer.
statement_title: Convergence under divergent descent-step parameters

conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local optimum}\Rightarrow D_S^\circ(x^*)\cap F_S(x^*)=\{0\};\quad\left(f\text{ is }f^\circ\text{-pseudoconvex}\land S\text{ is convex}\right)\Rightarrow\left(D_S^\circ(x^*)\cap F_S(x^*)=\{0\}\Rightarrow x^*\text{ global optimum}\right)
scope_note: Necessary constrained relaxed optimality condition, with global sufficiency under pseudoconvexity and convex feasibility.
statement_latex: Let \(S\ne\varnothing\), let \(x^*\in S\), and let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz at \(x^*\). If \(x^*\) is a local optimum of Problem (4.1), then \(D_S^\circ(x^*)\cap F_S(x^*)=\{0\}\). If, in addition, \(f\) is \(f^\circ\)-pseudoconvex and \(S\) is convex, this condition implies that \(x^*\) is a global optimum of Problem (4.1).
statement_plain: A constrained local optimum has no nonzero direction common to the specified relaxed descent and feasible-direction sets. For an f-circ-pseudoconvex objective over a convex feasible set, this condition is sufficient for global optimality.
statement_title: Relaxed Direction-Set Condition over a Convex Feasible Set

conclusion_latex: f\text{ is }f^\circ\text{-pseudoconvex}\iff \left(\forall x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ f^\circ(x;y-x)\geq0\implies f(y)\geq f(x)\right)
scope_note: Contrapositive reformulation of $f^\circ$-pseudoconvexity for locally Lipschitz functions.
statement_latex: A locally Lipschitz function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is $f^\circ$-pseudoconvex if and only if, for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $$f^\circ(x;y-x)\geq 0\implies f(y)\geq f(x).$$
statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz function is f-circ-pseudoconvex exactly when a nonnegative generalized directional derivative from x toward y implies that the value at y is no smaller than the value at x.
statement_title: Equivalent implication characterization of generalized pseudoconvexity

assumptions_latex: \text{Optimistic case: }x^0\in X\text{ is a weak global optimistic solution},\ y^0\in\widehat{\Psi}_o(x^0),\ F(x^0,y^0)=\bar{\varphi}_o(x^0),\ x\in O(y^0),\ F(x,y^0)\leq F(x^0,y^0)+\varepsilon

\text{Pessimistic case, respectively: }x^0\in X\text{ is a weak global pessimistic solution},\ y^0\in\widehat{\Psi}_p(x^0),\ F(x^0,y^0)=\bar{\varphi}_p(x^0),\ x\in P(y^0),\ F(x,y^0)\leq F(x^0,y^0)+\varepsilon
conclusion_latex: x\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-optimal in the corresponding optimistic or pessimistic case}
scope_note: Separate optimistic and pessimistic transfer guarantees based on a response attaining the auxiliary value.
statement_latex: Let \varepsilon>0. In the optimistic case, suppose x^0\in X is a weak global optimistic solution, y^0\in\widehat{\Psi}_o(x^0), and F(x^0,y^0)=\bar{\varphi}_o(x^0). Every x\in O(y^0) satisfying F(x,y^0)\leq F(x^0,y^0)+\varepsilon is then an \varepsilon\text{-optimal optimistic solution}. Respectively, if x^0\in X is a weak global pessimistic solution, y^0\in\widehat{\Psi}_p(x^0), and F(x^0,y^0)=\bar{\varphi}_p(x^0), then every x\in P(y^0) satisfying F(x,y^0)\leq F(x^0,y^0)+\varepsilon is an \varepsilon\text{-optimal pessimistic solution}.
statement_plain: Given a weak global optimistic or pessimistic solution and a corresponding response that attains its auxiliary value, any point in the matching set O(y0) or P(y0) whose objective is no more than epsilon above the reference objective is epsilon-optimal for that same case.
statement_title: Epsilon-Optimality Transfer from Weak Global Bilevel Solutions

conclusion_latex: H\text{ is quasidifferentiable at }x\iff H\text{ is directionally differentiable at }x\text{ and }H'_x(g)=\max_{A\in U}A(g)+\min_{B\in V}B(g)\ \forall g\in X\text{ for a quasidifferential class }[U,V];\quad \mathcal D(H_1+H_2)(x)=\mathcal DH_1(x)+\mathcal DH_2(x),\quad fH\text{ is quasidifferentiable at }x.
scope_note: Operator-valued quasidifferentiability, its support-set representation, and elementary closure properties.
statement_latex: Let $X$ be a Banach space, $\Omega\subset X$ be open, $Y$ be a Banach $K$-space, and $x\in\Omega$. A mapping $H:\Omega\to Y$ is quasidifferentiable at $x$ if it is directionally differentiable there and $H'_x$ is the sum of a continuous sublinear operator and a continuous superlinear operator. Its quasidifferential $\mathcal DH(x)$ is the corresponding equivalence class $[U,V]$ of support-set pairs satisfying $H'_x(g)=\max_{A\in U}A(g)+\min_{B\in V}B(g)$ for every $g\in X$. If $H_1$ and $H_2$ are quasidifferentiable at $x$, then $H_1+H_2$ is quasidifferentiable at $x$ and $\mathcal D(H_1+H_2)(x)=\mathcal DH_1(x)+\mathcal DH_2(x)$. If $H$ and a function $f$ are quasidifferentiable at $x$, then $fH$ is quasidifferentiable at $x$.
statement_plain: A mapping into a Banach K-space is quasidifferentiable when its directional derivative decomposes into continuous sublinear and superlinear parts. Its quasidifferential is the equivalence class of support-set pairs representing that derivative. Quasidifferentiability is preserved by addition and by multiplication of a quasidifferentiable mapping by a quasidifferentiable function.
statement_title: Quasidifferentiable Mappings into Banach K-Spaces

conclusion_latex: f(y)<f(x)\implies f^{\circ}(x;y-x)\leq0
scope_note: Locally Lipschitz generalized quasiconvexity using a strict value comparison and the Clarke generalized directional derivative.
statement_latex: A function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(l\)-quasiconvex if it is locally Lipschitz continuous and, for all \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[f(y)<f(x)\implies f^{\circ}(x;y-x)\leq0.\]
statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz function is l-quasiconvex if every direction toward a point with strictly smaller value has nonpositive Clarke generalized directional derivative.
statement_title: \(l\)-Quasiconvexity

conclusion_latex: Q\text{ is superlinear}\iff -Q\text{ is sublinear},\qquad \bar\partial Q=\{A:X\to Y\mid A\text{ is linear and }A(x)\ge Q(x)\ \forall x\in X\}.
scope_note: Order-dual counterpart of sublinear operators and their subdifferentials.
statement_latex: In the preceding setting, an operator \(Q:X\to Y\) is superlinear if \(-Q\) is sublinear. Its superdifferential is \(\bar\partial Q=\{A:X\to Y\mid A\text{ is linear and }A(x)\ge Q(x)\ \forall x\in X\}\).
statement_plain: An operator is superlinear when its negative is sublinear. Its superdifferential consists of all linear operators lying above it pointwise.
statement_title: Superlinear Operators and Superdifferentials

assumptions_latex: \text{At each nonterminal iteration, the system }M_ks_k=-f(x_k)\text{ can be solved}
conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\quad\text{at each nonterminal iteration}
scope_note: Finite-dimensional semismooth Newton iteration using a selected generalized derivative; the extract itself makes no convergence claim.
statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\) and set \(k=0\). If \(f(x_k)=0\), stop. Otherwise choose \(M_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), compute \(s_k\) from \(M_ks_k=-f(x_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), increment \(k\), and repeat.
statement_plain: Starting from an initial point, stop when the residual is zero. Otherwise select a generalized derivative, solve the associated Newton system, update the iterate, and repeat.
statement_title: Basic Semismooth Newton Iteration

assumptions_latex: S\text{ is the solution operator for }-\Delta y=u,\ y|_\Gamma=0
c>0\text{ when multiplier scaling is used}
conclusion_latex: u=P_{[u_a,u_b]}(-\lambda^{-1}p)\iff\text{the active/inactive relations hold};\quad A_n^a=A_{n-1}^a,\ A_n^b=A_{n-1}^b\Rightarrow u_n\text{ is optimal}.
scope_note: Infinite-dimensional active-set realization of the projection optimality condition, interpretable as semismooth Newton.
statement_latex: Let $S:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega)$ be the Dirichlet Poisson solution operator and minimize $f(u)=\frac12\|Su-y_\Omega\|_{L^2}^2+\frac\lambda2\|u\|_{L^2}^2$ over $U_{ad}=\{u:u_a\le u\le u_b\ \text{a.e.}\}$. With adjoint $p$ and $\mu=-(\lambda^{-1}p+u)$, optimality is equivalent to $u=P_{[u_a,u_b]}(-\lambda^{-1}p)$. Given arbitrary $u_0,\mu_0\in L^2(\Omega)$, define $A_n^b=\{u_{n-1}+\mu_{n-1}>u_b\}$, $A_n^a=\{u_{n-1}+\mu_{n-1}<u_a\}$, and $I_n=\Omega\setminus(A_n^a\cup A_n^b)$. Solve the coupled state-adjoint-control system with $u=u_a$ on $A_n^a$, $u=u_b$ on $A_n^b$, and $u=-\lambda^{-1}p$ on $I_n$, and set $\mu_n=-(\lambda^{-1}p_n+u_n)$. Terminate when both active sets are unchanged. Replacing $\mu$ by $c\mu$ for $c>0$ leaves the optimal case distinction unchanged.
statement_plain: Classify lower-active, upper-active, and inactive regions using the control plus a multiplier, solve the resulting coupled linear system, and stop when the active sets stabilize. The active-set relations are equivalent to the projection optimality condition, and the method admits a semismooth-Newton interpretation.
statement_title: Primal–Dual Active-Set Strategy for Box-Constrained Elliptic Control

assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is differentiable and convex}
h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is closed, proper, and convex}
conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{\ell(x;x_k)+h(x)+\frac12\|x-x_k\|_{H_k}^2\right\};\quad H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\Rightarrow\text{proximal Newton},\quad H_k=\alpha_k^{-1}I\Rightarrow\text{proximal gradient},\quad f\text{ positive-definite quadratic and }H_k=\nabla^2f\Rightarrow\text{one-step solution}.
scope_note: Positive-definite metric scaling of the composite proximal-gradient subproblem, including Newton and constrained-Newton special cases.
statement_latex:
Given \(H_k=H_k^\top\succ0\), define
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\ell(x;x_k)+h(x)+\frac12(x-x_k)^\top H_k(x-x_k)\right\}.
\]
Choosing \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\succ0\) gives proximal Newton, while \(H_k=\alpha_k^{-1}I\) gives ordinary proximal gradient. If \(h=\delta_X\), the Hessian choice gives constrained Newton; if additionally \(X=\mathbb R^n\), it gives classical Newton. If \(f\) is a positive-definite quadratic and \(H_k=\nabla^2f\), the unit-step method solves the composite problem in one iteration.
statement_plain: Variable-metric proximal gradient replaces the scalar quadratic regularizer by a positive-definite matrix. A Hessian metric produces proximal Newton, an inverse-stepsize identity metric recovers proximal gradient, and an indicator term produces constrained Newton. For a positive-definite quadratic smooth term with the exact Hessian, a unit step reaches the composite optimum in one iteration. Diagonal and quasi-Newton metrics are possible, but descent and superlinear convergence require additional conditions not specified in the extract.
statement_title: Variable-metric proximal-gradient and proximal-Newton iteration

assumptions_latex: \forall n\in\{1,\ldots,N\}:\ Y_n\subset\mathbb R^m\text{ is closed and convex, and }\mathbb R_-^m\subset Y_n.
\forall n:\ u_n:Y_n\to\mathbb R\text{ is concave and upper semicontinuous}.
conclusion_latex: \exists\bar p\ge0\text{ dual-optimal such that }\forall n,\ \bar y_n\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y_n}\left(u_n(y)+\langle\bar p,y\rangle\right),\qquad\sum_{n=1}^N\bar y_n+c\ge0.
scope_note: Separable concave resource allocation across factories coupled by aggregate resource constraints.
statement_latex: For \(n=1,\ldots,N\), let \(Y_n\subset\mathbb R^m\) be closed and convex with \(\mathbb R_-^m\subset Y_n\), and let \(u_n:Y_n\to\mathbb R\) be concave and upper semicontinuous. If \(\left(\sum_{n=1}^N Y_n\right)\cap\left(-c+\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+^m\right)\ne\varnothing\), then the dual problem \[\inf_{p\ge0}\left\{\sum_{n=1}^N\sup_{y\in Y_n}\left[u_n(y)+\langle p,y\rangle\right]+\langle p,c\rangle\right\}\] has a solution \(\bar p\). If the centralized problem has a unique optimizer \((\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_N)\), then \[\bar y_n\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y_n}\left[u_n(y)+\langle\bar p,y\rangle\right]\quad(n=1,\ldots,N).\] Thus the independently selected factory decisions reproduce the feasible allocation maximizing total real profit.
statement_plain: Under the stated convexity, upper-semicontinuity, and strict aggregate-feasibility assumptions, optimal nonnegative shadow prices exist. If the centralized optimum is unique, each factory recovers its component independently by maximizing real profit plus shadow-valued net production.
statement_title: Decentralization by optimal shadow prices

statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a closed subset of a Banach space and let \(T:S\to S\) be continuous. If \(T^n\) is a contraction mapping for some positive integer \(n\), then \(T\) has a unique fixed point in \(S\), which can be found by successive approximation.
statement_plain: If a continuous self-map of a closed subset of a Banach space has a contractive positive iterate, then the original map has a unique fixed point obtainable by successive approximation.
statement_title: Fixed Point from a Contractive Iterate

scope_note: Commodity-wise balance constraints in which only agents carrying a given commodity component participate; notation is normalized to resolve inconsistent indices in the extract.
statement_latex:
Let \(c_i\subseteq [n]\) be the commodity components carried by agent \(i\), and define the participating-agent set for commodity \(k\) by
\[
I_k:=\{i\in[N]:k\in c_i\}.
\]
The general-form exchange constraint set is
\[
\mathcal C=\left\{(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\;\middle|\;\sum_{i\in I_k}(z_i)_k=0\quad\text{for every }k\in[n]\right\}.
\]
If \(I_k=[N]\) for every commodity \(k\), this reduces to the global exchange formulation.
statement_plain: For each commodity, the corresponding components must sum to zero over the agents that carry that commodity. When every agent participates in every commodity exchange, the formulation reduces to global exchange.
statement_title: General-form exchange constraint set

statement_latex: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space. A map $f:X\to X$ is a contraction if there exists $\alpha\in[0,1)$ such that, for all $x,y\in X$, $d(f(x),f(y))\leq \alpha d(x,y)$.
statement_plain: A self-map of a metric space is a contraction if one common factor alpha, strictly less than one, bounds the reduction of every pairwise distance.
statement_title: Contraction Mapping

statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, let \(T:C\to C\), and choose \(x^0\in C\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and an iteration limit \(K\in\mathbb{N}\). statement_plain: Picard iteration repeatedly applies the mapping without relaxation and stops when its fixed-point residual reaches the tolerance or the iteration limit is reached.

scope_note: Equality of primal and Lagrangian-dual optimal values under strict primal feasibility.

statement_plain: For a convex optimization problem with affine equalities, Slater strict feasibility implies zero Lagrangian duality gap.
