assumptions_latex: \widetilde{\mathbf A}=m^{-1/2}\mathbf A,\quad \mathbf A\text{ is a random }m\times N\text{ Gaussian matrix}
conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left(\forall\mathbf e\in\mathbb C^m:\ \|\mathbf x-\Delta_1(\widetilde{\mathbf A}\mathbf x+\mathbf e)\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\sigma_s(\mathbf x)_p+D s_*^{1/q-1/2}\|\mathbf e\|_2\right)\ge1-5e^{-c_1m}.
scope_note: Fixed-signal recovery in \(\ell_q\), controlled by best \(s\)-term \(\ell_p\) approximation and uniform over additive noise vectors.
statement_latex: There exist universal constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3,C,D>0\) such that, for \(1\le p\le q\le2\), every fixed \(\mathbf x\in\mathbb C^N\), and \(\widetilde{\mathbf A}=m^{-1/2}\mathbf A\), where \(\mathbf A\) is a random draw of an \(m\times N\) Gaussian matrix, if \(N\ge c_2m\) and \(s\le c_3s_*\), with \(s_*=m/\ln(eN/m)\), then with probability at least \(1-5e^{-c_1m}\), simultaneously for all \(\mathbf e\in\mathbb C^m\), \[\left\|\mathbf x-\Delta_1(\widetilde{\mathbf A}\mathbf x+\mathbf e)\right\|_q\le \frac{C}{s^{1/p-1/q}}\sigma_s(\mathbf x)_p+D s_*^{1/q-1/2}\|\mathbf e\|_2.\]
statement_plain: For 1≤p≤q≤2 and every fixed signal, a normalized Gaussian measurement matrix satisfies, with probability at least 1−5 exp(−c₁m), an ℓq recovery bound simultaneously for every noise vector under the stated dimensional and sparsity conditions.
statement_title: Nonuniform Gaussian ℓp-to-ℓq instance-optimal recovery

assumptions_latex: (\cdot)_N\text{ is defined using the componentwise minimization order}
conclusion_latex: (\alpha\mathcal Y)_N=\alpha(\mathcal Y_N).
scope_note: The equality is restricted to strictly positive real scaling; zero and negative scalars are excluded.
statement_latex: For \(\mathcal Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) with \(\alpha>0\), \[(\alpha\mathcal Y)_N=\alpha(\mathcal Y_N).\]
statement_plain: Scaling an objective set by a strictly positive scalar scales its nondominated set by the same scalar.
statement_title: Positive scaling of nondominated sets

conclusion_latex: \mathbf x\text{ is the unique minimizer of }\{\|\mathbf z\|_1:\mathbf A\mathbf z=\mathbf A\mathbf x\}\iff\ker(\mathbf A)\cap T(\mathbf x)=\{\mathbf0\}
scope_note: Characterizes unique recovery of an individual vector by equality-constrained basis pursuit; the notation \(T(\mathbf x)\) is retained from the source extract.
statement_latex: For \(\mathbf A\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\) and \(\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^N\), the vector \(\mathbf x\) is the unique minimizer of \(\|\mathbf z\|_1\) subject to \(\mathbf A\mathbf z=\mathbf A\mathbf x\) if and only if \(\ker(\mathbf A)\cap T(\mathbf x)=\{\mathbf 0\}\).
statement_plain: A vector is the unique equality-constrained basis-pursuit solution if and only if the measurement nullspace intersects its associated cone only at zero.
statement_title: Nullspace–cone criterion for unique basis-pursuit recovery

assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\text{ is Gaussian or Bernoulli}
conclusion_latex: \mathbb P\!\left(\delta_s(A/\sqrt m)\le\delta\right)\ge1-\varepsilon.
scope_note: Universal-constant RIP bound for normalized Gaussian or random-sign measurements.
statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\) be a Gaussian or Bernoulli random matrix. There exists a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, whenever \[m\ge C\delta^{-2}\left(s\log\frac{eN}{s}+\log\frac{2}{\varepsilon}\right),\] the normalized matrix satisfies \(\delta_s(A/\sqrt m)\le\delta\) with probability at least \(1-\varepsilon\).
statement_plain: A normalized Gaussian or Bernoulli random matrix satisfies the order-s restricted-isometry bound with probability at least one minus epsilon when its number of rows meets the stated universal-constant sample bound.
statement_title: Restricted isometry of Gaussian and Bernoulli matrices

assumptions_latex: \mathcal S\text{ is a convex constraint system in }(y,\alpha,u)
conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_{y,\alpha}\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S)\subseteq\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC})
scope_note: Defines safety by projected feasible-set containment and tractability by efficient computability of the convex constraint system.
statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal S\) be a system of convex constraints in \(y\), \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_S)\ge 0\), and possibly auxiliary variables \(u\). It is a safe approximation of the given globalized robust counterpart \(\mathrm{GRC}\) if
\[
\forall (y,\alpha),\quad \bigl[\exists u:\ (y,\alpha,u)\in\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S)\bigr]\Rightarrow (y,\alpha)\in\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{proj}_{y,\alpha}\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S)\subseteq\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}).
\]
The approximation is tractable when \(\mathcal S\) is tractable, for example when it is an explicit system of conic quadratic inequalities or linear matrix inequalities, or more generally when its constraints are efficiently computable.
statement_plain: A convex lifted system safely approximates a given globalized robust counterpart when every feasible point projected from the lifted system is feasible for that counterpart. The approximation is tractable when the convex constraint system is efficiently computable, as with explicit conic quadratic inequalities or linear matrix inequalities.
statement_title: Safe and Tractable Approximation of a Globalized Robust Counterpart

conclusion_latex: \left[\forall i\in\{0,\ldots,m\},\ f_i\text{ is convex}\right]\Longrightarrow \text{the stated problem is a convex optimization problem},\qquad \mathrm{LP}\subseteq\{\text{convex optimization problems}\}.
scope_note: Finite-dimensional inequality-form convex programs; this formulation does not address equality constraints or extended-valued functions.
statement_latex: The problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f_0(x)\) subject to \(f_i(x)\le b_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), is called a convex optimization problem when each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(i=0,\ldots,m\), is convex, i.e., for every \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\alpha,\beta\ge 0\) with \(\alpha+\beta=1\), \[f_i(\alpha x+\beta y)\le \alpha f_i(x)+\beta f_i(y).\] Every linear function satisfies this relation with equality; consequently, every linear program is a convex optimization problem.
statement_plain: An inequality-form optimization problem is convex when its objective and all its constraint functions satisfy the convexity inequality for every convex combination of two points. Linear functions satisfy that relation with equality, so every linear program belongs to the class of convex optimization problems.
statement_title: Convex Optimization Problem and Inclusion of Linear Programs

assumptions_latex: (\mathcal Z,\mathcal L,\|\cdot\|)\text{ is a perturbation structure}
conclusion_latex: x\text{ is globally robust feasible with sensitivity }\alpha\iff\left(a^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell a^\ell\right)^Tx\leq b^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell b^\ell+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\mathcal Z\mid\mathcal L)\quad\forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z_+.
scope_note: Defines global robust feasibility with prescribed sensitivity through a semi-infinite family of relaxed uncertain linear inequalities.
statement_latex:
Given \(\alpha\geq0\) and a perturbation structure \((\mathcal Z,\mathcal L,\|\cdot\|)\), a vector \(x\) is globally robust feasible with global sensitivity \(\alpha\) for the uncertain linear constraint precisely when
\[
\left(a^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell a^\ell\right)^Tx
\leq b^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell b^\ell
+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\mathcal Z\mid\mathcal L)
\quad\text{for every }\zeta\in\mathcal Z_+=\mathcal Z+\mathcal L.
\]
This semi-infinite constraint is called the globalized robust counterpart of the uncertain linear constraint.
statement_plain: A vector is globally robust feasible with sensitivity alpha when the uncertain linear inequality holds for every physically possible perturbation after allowing a relaxation equal to alpha times its cone-compatible distance from the normal perturbation range. This semi-infinite family is the globalized robust counterpart.
statement_title: Globalized Robust Counterpart of an Uncertain Linear Constraint

assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is closed, proper, and convex}
conclusion_latex: \forall z\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \operatorname{prox}(z\mid f)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{f(u)+\tfrac12\lVert z-u\rVert^2\},\quad \operatorname{prox}(z\mid f^*)=z-\operatorname{prox}(z\mid f).
scope_note: Definition of the unit-parameter Euclidean proximal mapping together with the conjugate-side Moreau identity.
statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be closed, proper, and convex. For each \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\), there is a unique decomposition
\[
z=x+x^*,\qquad x^*\in\partial f(x).
\]
The component \(x\), equivalently the unique minimizer of
\[
\inf_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(u)+\tfrac12\lVert z-u\rVert^2\right\},
\]
is denoted \(\operatorname{prox}(z\mid f)\), and \(z\mapsto\operatorname{prox}(z\mid f)\) is the proximation corresponding to \(f\). Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{prox}(z\mid f^*)=z-\operatorname{prox}(z\mid f)\qquad(\forall z\in\mathbb{R}^n).
\]
statement_plain: The proximal mapping of a closed proper convex function sends each vector to the unique minimizer of the function plus one half the squared Euclidean distance. It is the primal component of the unique subgradient decomposition, and the proximal mappings of the function and its conjugate sum to the identity.
statement_title: Proximal mapping and conjugate proximal decomposition

conclusion_latex: p(x)=\det\!\left(L_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iL_i\right),\quad L_i=L_i^{\mathsf T};\qquad L_0\succ0\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{the representation is monic}.
scope_note: Defines symmetric determinantal representations of real polynomials and records the stated existence of a possibly nonmonic symmetric linear-pencil representation.
statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), a symmetric determinantal representation is an identity \(p(x)=\det L(x)\), where \(L(x)=L_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iL_i\) and every \(L_i\) is symmetric. Such a representation is called monic when \(L_0\succ0\). Moreover, every real polynomial can be expressed as the determinant of a symmetric linear pencil, although the pencil need not be monic.
statement_plain: A symmetric determinantal representation expresses a real polynomial as the determinant of an affine linear matrix pencil with symmetric coefficient matrices. It is called monic when the constant matrix is positive definite. Every real polynomial has such a linear-pencil representation, but it need not be monic.
statement_title: Symmetric and Monic Symmetric Determinantal Representations

assumptions_latex: \text{At every simplex iteration, the leaving variable is selected by the lexicographic rule.}
conclusion_latex: \text{The simplex method terminates.}
scope_note: Finite termination of the simplex method under lexicographic leaving-variable selection.
statement_latex: \text{If the leaving variable is selected by the lexicographic rule at every simplex iteration, then the simplex method terminates.}
statement_plain: The simplex method terminates if the leaving variable is selected by the lexicographic rule at every iteration.
statement_title: Termination Under the Lexicographic Leaving Rule

conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists h_0>0\;\forall\varepsilon\in(0,h_0):f(\varepsilon)>0\bigr)\iff\bigl(f\not\equiv0\ \land\ a_{\min\{i:a_i\ne0\}}>0\bigr)
scope_note: Local sign criterion used in infinitesimal symbolic perturbation.
statement_latex: Let \(f(\varepsilon)=\sum_{i=0}^{m}a_i\varepsilon^i\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb R\). There exists \(h_0>0\) such that \(f(\varepsilon)>0\) for every \(0<\varepsilon<h_0\) if and only if \(f\not\equiv0\) and its lowest-degree nonzero coefficient is positive.
statement_plain: A real polynomial is positive for all sufficiently small positive epsilon exactly when it is nonzero and its lowest-degree nonzero coefficient is positive.
statement_title: Sign of a Polynomial Near Zero

assumptions_latex: \text{The constraint system is that of the classical transportation problem.}
conclusion_latex: \text{Every transportation basis is triangular.}
scope_note: Structural property of bases in the classical transportation tableau.
statement_latex: Every basis of the classical transportation problem is triangular in the transportation-tableau sense.
statement_plain: All bases of the classical transportation problem are triangular.
statement_title: Triangularity of Transportation Bases

conclusion_latex: \exists p^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{p\ge0}g(p)\quad\text{such that}\quad g(p^\star)=c^{\mathsf T}x^\star
scope_note: States dual attainment and equality of optimal values for the LP pair obtained by dualizing Ax≥b and retaining x∈P.
statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x\mid Ax\ge b,\ x\in P\},\qquad
\max_{p\ge0}g(p),
\]
where \(P=\{x\mid Dx\ge d\}\) and
\[
g(p)=\min_{x\in P}\bigl[c^{\mathsf T}x+p^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\bigr].
\]
If the primal problem has an optimal solution \(x^\star\), then the dual has an optimal solution \(p^\star\), and
\[
g(p^\star)=c^{\mathsf T}x^\star.
\]
statement_plain: If the partially dualized linear program has a primal optimal solution, then its dual also attains an optimum, and the primal and dual optimal values are equal.
statement_title: Strong duality for a partially dualized linear program

assumptions_latex: r_k\text{ is a ratio used in the leaving-variable calculation.}
\text{Ratios with positive numerator and zero denominator are assigned the extended-real value }+\infty.
conclusion_latex: \left(\exists k:\operatorname{num}(r_k)>0\land\operatorname{den}(r_k)=0\right)\Longrightarrow\left(\exists k:r_k=+\infty\right)\Longrightarrow\text{the pivot is degenerate}.
scope_note: Operational definition under the source's extended-real leaving-ratio convention. It does not assert that every degenerate dictionary produces a degenerate pivot.
statement_latex: Under the leaving-variable ratio convention, a pivot is called degenerate if at least one calculated ratio equals \(+\infty\); this occurs when that ratio has a positive numerator and a zero denominator.
statement_plain: Under the stated ratio convention, a pivot is degenerate when at least one leaving-variable ratio is positive infinity, arising from a positive numerator and a zero denominator.
statement_title: Infinite-Ratio Criterion for a Degenerate Pivot

assumptions_latex: x_{\ell_j}\text{ is a nonbasic variable represented in the simplex tableau.}
conclusion_latex: r_j\text{ has been computed}\Rightarrow x_{\ell_j}\text{ is priced.}
scope_note: Explicit-column entering-variable selection and computation of tableau coefficients used for that selection.
statement_latex: The process of selecting the entering variable during a simplex pivot is sometimes called pricing. A nonbasic variable \(x_{\ell_j}\) is said to be priced when its coefficient \(r_j\) in the last row of the simplex tableau has been computed.
statement_plain: Selecting the entering variable for a simplex pivot is sometimes called pricing. A nonbasic variable is priced when its coefficient in the tableau's last row has been computed.
statement_title: Simplex pricing

assumptions_latex: P_j^{(k)}\in C_j\text{ is a specified column available at stage }k
conclusion_latex: \text{The restricted-master optimum determines multipliers }\pi=\pi^0\text{ for the subprograms.}
scope_note: Stagewise restricted master for column generation using the currently specified columns from the coefficient sets.
statement_latex: At stage k, the restricted master program has variables x_j^{(k)} associated with specified columns P_j^{(k)}\in C_j. Its optimal solution determines simplex multipliers \pi=\pi^0 for use in the subprograms.
statement_plain: At stage k, the restricted master uses the currently specified columns drawn from the sets C_j. Solving it determines the simplex multipliers used in the subprograms.
statement_title: Restricted Master Program at an Algorithmic Stage

assumptions_latex: A root is fixed throughout the network-simplex iterations.
The current tree is strongly feasible.
When leaving candidates are tied, the join-based first-candidate rule is used.
conclusion_latex: T\text{ strongly feasible}\Longrightarrow T+e-f\text{ strongly feasible}\Longrightarrow\text{network simplex does not cycle.}
scope_note: Defines strong feasibility, describes its construction-or-decomposition procedure, and states the invariant-preserving anti-cycling tie rule.
statement_latex: Fix a root. A feasible tree solution $(T,x)$ is strongly feasible if every tree arc $ij$ with $x_{ij}=0$ is directed away from the root. The artificial-arc initial tree is strongly feasible. Given any feasible tree defining $x$, a zero-flow tree arc directed toward the root can be replaced by an appropriate oppositely directed crossing arc while preserving $x$; iterating either yields a strongly feasible tree defining $x$ or exposes a balanced cut that decomposes the problem. Starting from a strongly feasible tree, let $e$ be any entering arc, let $C$ be its fundamental cycle, and let the join be the first common node on the two endpoint-to-root paths. If leaving candidates are tied, choose the first candidate encountered while traversing $C$ in the direction of $e$ from the join. This rule preserves strong feasibility for both degenerate and nondegenerate pivots. Therefore, beginning with a strongly feasible tree and applying this leaving rule prevents cycling without restricting the entering-arc choice.
statement_plain: A rooted feasible tree is strongly feasible when every zero-flow tree arc points away from the root. A feasible tree can be converted to this form unless the conversion exposes a balanced decomposition. During a pivot, resolve a leaving-arc tie by taking the first candidate on the fundamental cycle when traversing from the join in the entering arc's direction. This preserves strong feasibility and prevents cycling regardless of the entering-arc rule.
statement_title: Strongly feasible trees and Cunningham's leaving-arc rule

assumptions_latex: y\text{ is the current revised-simplex multiplier row}
conclusion_latex: \max_{a\in\mathbb Z_+^m:\,\sum_iw_i a_i\le r}y^Ta>1\iff\text{an improving entering pattern exists.}
scope_note: Cutting-stock specialization of column generation as implicit-column revised simplex.
statement_latex: Let \(r>0\), let \(w_i>0\), and let \(b_i\in\mathbb Z_+\) be the required quantities. A cutting pattern is \(a\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i a_i\le r\). For the master LP \(\min\{\mathbf 1^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), after computing the revised-simplex multiplier \(y\), solve \(\max\{y^Ta:\sum_iw_i a_i\le r,\ a\in\mathbb Z_+^m\}\). A negative-reduced-cost entering pattern exists if and only if the pricing value exceeds \(1\); otherwise no improving pattern exists.
statement_plain: Columns are feasible integer cutting patterns. Revised simplex need not enumerate them: each iteration solves an integer knapsack pricing problem, admitting a pattern when its dual value exceeds its unit cost.
statement_title: Delayed column generation for the cutting-stock relaxation

assumptions_latex: \widetilde w\text{ is a specified final target}
\text{A sequence of intermediate targets is available}
conclusion_latex: (x,w)\text{ is updated by nested target-advancement and Newton-correction loops toward }\widetilde w.
scope_note: Nested target advancement and primal Newton correction; the target sequence, closeness tests, termination, and convergence guarantees are unspecified.
statement_latex: \text{Given primal-feasible }x^0=x(w^0)\text{ and a final target }\widetilde w,\ (x,w)\leftarrow(x^0,w^0).\ \text{While }w\text{ is not close to }\widetilde w,\text{ select the next target }w\text{ and apply Newton steps at }x\text{ for }w\text{ until }x\text{ is close to }x(w).
statement_plain: Initialize at the primal-feasible target point x⁰=x(w⁰). Repeatedly advance to the next target and apply primal Newton steps until the iterate is close to its target point. The extract does not specify the target sequence, closeness tests, termination, or convergence.
statement_title: Generic primal target-following Newton algorithm

conclusion_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\iff A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
scope_note: Positive-definite-pivot Schur-complement form of block matrix elimination.
statement_latex:
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(A\in\mathbb S^p\), \(C\in\mathbb S^q\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\), and \(C\succ0\). Then
\[
M\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.
\]
Thus the block associated with \(C\) can be eliminated exactly, yielding the Schur-complement inequality. The strict assumption \(C\succ0\) ensures that \(C^{-1}\) exists; singular pivots require a generalized-inverse condition together with a range constraint.
statement_plain: With a positive definite pivot block, a block PSD constraint is exactly equivalent to positivity of its Schur complement.
statement_title: Matrix-Elimination Principles

assumptions_latex: \Sigma\text{ is a solution of the SDP relaxation of MAXCUT}
conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\zeta^\top L\zeta]\ge 0.878\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}x^\top Lx
scope_note: Expected approximation guarantee from Gaussian sign rounding of an optimal MAXCUT SDP solution.
statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma\) be a solution of the SDP relaxation of MAXCUT, let \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\), and set \(\zeta=\operatorname{sign}(\xi)\in\{-1,1\}^n\). Then \[\mathbb E[\zeta^\top L\zeta]\ge 0.878\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}x^\top Lx.\]
statement_plain: Gaussian sign rounding of an optimal MAXCUT SDP solution achieves an expected objective value at least 0.878 times the optimal discrete MAXCUT objective.
statement_title: Gaussian Sign-Rounding Guarantee for MAXCUT

assumptions_latex: (P)\text{ is a conic convex optimization problem over }K
conclusion_latex: \bigl((P)\text{ admits a symmetric }v\Leftrightarrow\text{-space construction}\bigr)\iff\bigl(K\text{ is homogeneous and self-dual}\bigr).
scope_note: Characterizes existence of the symmetric scaling construction by homogeneous self-dual cone geometry.
statement_latex: A conic convex optimization problem \((P)\) over \(K\) admits a symmetric \(v\Leftrightarrow\)-space construction if and only if \(K\) is a homogeneous self-dual cone.
statement_plain: A conic convex problem has the symmetric scaling-space construction exactly when its cone is homogeneous and self-dual.
statement_title: Characterization of Symmetric \(v\Leftrightarrow\)-Space Constructions

assumptions_latex: W\text{ is defined as in the preceding construction}
conclusion_latex: \|W\|\geq\frac{\sqrt3}{2\lambda}
scope_note: Extraction-grounded analytic lemma for the SDP potential-reduction construction; \(W\) is referenced exactly as defined in the preceding construction.
statement_latex: Given \(X,S\in\mathcal S_{++}^n\) and \(T\in\mathcal T(X,S)\), let \(V:=T(S)\), let \(W\) be as defined in the preceding potential-reduction construction, and let \(\lambda\) be the associated scaling parameter. Then \[\|W\|\geq\frac{\sqrt3}{2\lambda}.\]
statement_plain: The norm of the quantity W from the preceding scaled potential construction is at least square root of three divided by twice the associated scaling parameter.
statement_title: Lower bound for the scaled potential quantity

assumptions_latex: Q=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\langle a_i,x\rangle\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\text{ is a convex polytope}
conclusion_latex: W(H,v)=\{x:\langle H^{-1}(x-v),x-v\rangle\le1\},\qquad W^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\substack{E\subseteq Q\\E\text{ ellipsoid centered at }v}}\operatorname{vol}_n(E).
scope_note: Definition and shape-matrix representation for ellipsoids centered at a fixed interior point of a polytope.
statement_latex: Let Q=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\langle a_i,x\rangle\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\} be a convex polytope and let v\in\operatorname{int}Q. For H\in\operatorname{int}\mathbb S_+^n, define W(H,v)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\langle H^{-1}(x-v),x-v\rangle\le1\}. A maximum-volume ellipsoid in Q centered at v is an ellipsoid W^\star\subseteq Q, centered at v, whose volume is maximal among all ellipsoids centered at v and contained in Q.
statement_plain: Fix an interior point of a polytope. Positive-definite shape matrices describe ellipsoids centered there, and a maximum-volume centered inscribed ellipsoid is one attaining the largest volume among all centered ellipsoids contained in the polytope.
statement_title: Maximum-Volume Inscribed Ellipsoid with Prescribed Center

assumptions_latex: \(\left(y^*,X^*,\tau^*,\vartheta^*,S^*,\rho^*,\nu^*\right)\) is an optimal solution of the embedding problem.
conclusion_latex: \(X^*\) and \(S^*\) have largest possible rank, and as many scalar variables as possible are strictly positive.
scope_note: Defines maximal complementarity relative to the optimal solutions of the specified embedding problem.
statement_latex: An optimal solution \(\left(y^*,X^*,\tau^*,\vartheta^*,S^*,\rho^*,\nu^*\right)\) of the embedding problem is called maximally complementary if \(X^*\) and \(S^*\) have largest possible rank and as many of its scalar variables as possible are strictly positive.
statement_plain: An optimal embedding solution is maximally complementary if its matrix variables X and S have largest possible rank and as many scalar variables as possible are strictly positive.
statement_title: Maximally Complementary Embedding Solution

assumptions_latex: F_k\text{ is an analytic barrier of }E_k
conclusion_latex: V_k(x)=\ln\det\nabla^2F_k(x),\qquad y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{int}(E_k)}V_k(x).
scope_note: Definition induced by the Hessian determinant of an analytic barrier on a polytope with nonempty interior.
statement_latex: Let E_k be a polytope with \operatorname{int}(E_k)\neq\varnothing, and let F_k be an analytic barrier for E_k. Define V_k(x)=\ln\det\nabla^2F_k(x) for x\in\operatorname{int}(E_k). The function V_k is the volumetric barrier, and any y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{int}(E_k)}V_k(x) is a volumetric center.
statement_plain: For a polytope with nonempty interior and analytic barrier F_k, the volumetric barrier is the logarithm of the determinant of the Hessian of F_k. Any minimizer of this function over the polytope's interior is a volumetric center.
statement_title: Volumetric Barrier and Volumetric Center

assumptions_latex: \(\delta>0\) is selected as specified by the associated short-step theorem.
conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k=1,\qquad \sigma_k=1-\delta/\sqrt n\quad\text{for all }k\ge0.\)
scope_note: Short-step specialization of the primal-dual SDP path-following framework.
statement_latex: For every iteration \(k\ge0\), take the full step \(\alpha_k=1\) and choose \(\sigma_k=1-\delta/\sqrt n\), where \(\delta>0\) is selected according to the associated short-step theorem.
statement_plain: At every iteration, the SDP short-step method takes a full step and uses the centrality parameter one minus delta divided by the square root of the matrix dimension.
statement_title: Full-Step SDP Short-Step Parameter Rule

assumptions_latex: \varphi_k\text{ and }\mathcal W_k\text{ satisfy the referenced bundle-model admissibility conditions}
conclusion_latex: \text{The method takes serious or null steps according to the actual-versus-predicted decrease test and stops when }f(x_k)-\varphi_k(y_{k+1})\leq\delta(|f(x_k)|+1).
scope_note: Proximal bundle iteration for minimizing the maximum-eigenvalue objective using leading-eigenvector information.
statement_latex:
Given $x_0\in\mathbb R^m$, $\delta>0$, $m_L\in(0,1/2)$, $\mu_0>0$, a prescribed minimal weight $\mu_{\min}$, and $M_0\succ0$, compute $f(x_0)$, a normalized leading eigenvector of $C-\mathcal A^Tx_0$, and an admissible initial model. At iteration $k$, solve
\[y_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{\varphi_k(y)+\frac{\mu_k}{2}\|y-x_k\|_k^2\right\}.\]
Evaluate $f(y_{k+1})$ and a normalized, possibly $\epsilon$-approximate, leading eigenvector of $C-\mathcal A^Ty_{k+1}$, and update the admissible model. Stop when
\[f(x_k)-\varphi_k(y_{k+1})\leq\delta\bigl(|f(x_k)|+1\bigr).\]
If
\[f(x_k)-f(y_{k+1})\geq m_L\bigl(f(x_k)-\varphi_k(y_{k+1})\bigr),\]
set $x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}$, choose $\mu_{k+1}\in[\mu_{\min},\mu_k]$, and choose the next metric. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k$ and choose $\mu_{k+1}\in[\mu_k,10\mu_k]$.
statement_plain: Each iteration minimizes the current spectral bundle model plus a quadratic proximal term, evaluates the maximum-eigenvalue objective and leading-eigenvector information, and updates the model. A candidate producing the required fraction of predicted decrease is accepted as a serious step; otherwise the method takes a null step. The stated relative model-gap test terminates the iteration.
statement_title: General serious/null-step spectral bundle method

assumptions_latex: (y^*,X^*,\tau^*,\vartheta^*,S^*,\rho^*,\nu^*)\text{ is a maximally complementary solution of the embedding.}
X(\mu),\tau(\mu)\text{ are embedded-central-path variables in the branch }\tau^*=\rho^*=0.
conclusion_latex: \tau^*>0\Rightarrow\text{the extract identifies }S^*/\tau^*\text{ as optimal for }(D);\quad \rho^*>0\Rightarrow\text{strong infeasibility of }(P),(D),\text{ or both is detected};\quad \tau^*=\rho^*=0\Rightarrow\lim_{\mu\to0}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\frac{CX(\mu)}{\tau(\mu)}\right)=\begin{cases}d^*,&d^*\text{ is finite},\\+\infty,&(D)\text{ is weakly infeasible},\\+\infty,&\text{the source's truncated unboundedness condition holds.}\end{cases}
scope_note: Extraction-grounded summary. The source truncates one unboundedness condition in the limiting classification; that condition remains explicitly unresolved. The source also states recovery of $S^*/\tau^*$ alone as an optimal solution of $(D)$, although the displayed formulation has variables $(y,S)$; no missing component is inferred.
statement_latex: For $(D)$, solve its self-dual embedding together with its Lagrangean dual $(P)$ to obtain a maximally complementary embedding solution $(y^*,X^*,\tau^*,\vartheta^*,S^*,\rho^*,\nu^*)$. If $\tau^*>0$, the extract states that $S^*/\tau^*$ is an optimal solution of $(D)$. If $\rho^*>0$, strong infeasibility of $(P)$, $(D)$, or both is detected. If $\tau^*=\rho^*=0$, solve the embedding of the extended Lagrange--Slater dual $(P_{gf})$ and its Lagrangean dual by following the embedded central path. The resulting trace limit equals $d^*$ when $d^*$ is finite and is $+\infty$ when $(D)$ is weakly infeasible; the extract also assigns $+\infty$ under a truncated condition beginning that $(D)$ is "unbounded without an ...".
statement_plain: Solve the SDP self-dual embedding and inspect its scaling variables. Positive tau yields the optimal object stated in the extract, positive rho detects strong infeasibility, and the case tau equals rho equals zero invokes an extended embedding and its central path. The trace limit equals the finite optimal value and diverges for weak infeasibility, as well as for an additional unboundedness case whose condition is truncated.
statement_title: Self-dual-embedding procedure for determining SDP status

conclusion_latex: (\mathrm{CDT1})\text{ is polynomial-time solvable and }\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{CDT1})=\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{SDP\ relaxation}).
scope_note: Strictly feasible instances of the named CDT1 problem class.
statement_latex: If \((\mathrm{CDT1})\) is strictly feasible, then \((\mathrm{CDT1})\) can be solved in polynomial time and its SDP relaxation has zero relaxation gap.
statement_plain: A strictly feasible CDT1 instance is polynomial-time solvable, and its semidefinite relaxation preserves the optimal value.
statement_title: Polynomial solvability and exact SDP relaxation of CDT1

conclusion_latex: A\succ0\iff(\forall x\neq0)\ x^TAx>0\iff(\forall i)\ \lambda_i(A)>0\iff(\forall k=1,\ldots,n)\det A_{\{1,\ldots,k\}}>0\iff(\forall k=0,\ldots,n-1)\ (-1)^{n-k}p_k>0\iff(\exists B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ nonsingular})\ A=BB^T.
scope_note: Equivalent full-space strict-curvature criteria for a real symmetric matrix.
statement_latex: For A\in\mathcal S^n, the following are equivalent: (i) A\succ0; (ii) x^TAx>0 for every nonzero x\in\mathbb R^n; (iii) every eigenvalue of A is strictly positive; (iv) all n leading principal minors are strictly positive; (v) if p_A(\lambda)=\lambda^n+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p_k\lambda^k, then (-1)^{n-k}p_k>0 for k=0,\ldots,n-1; and (vi) A=BB^T for a square nonsingular matrix B.
statement_plain: A real symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when its quadratic form is positive away from the origin, its eigenvalues are positive, its leading principal minors are positive, its characteristic-polynomial coefficients strictly alternate in sign, or it has a nonsingular square Gram factor.
statement_title: Equivalent criteria for positive definiteness

conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda^{\mathrm M}\in\mathbb R:\ (H+\lambda^{\mathrm M}I)s^{\mathrm M}=-g,\quad H+\lambda^{\mathrm M}I\succeq0;\qquad H+\lambda^{\mathrm M}I\succ0\implies s^{\mathrm M}\text{ is the unique global minimizer on }\{s:\|s\|_2=\Delta\}.
scope_note: Necessary conditions and a uniqueness criterion for the equality-boundary Euclidean trust-region subproblem.
statement_latex: Let \(q(s)=q_0+g^\top s+\tfrac12s^\top Hs\), where \(H=H^\top\), and let \(\Delta>0\). If \(s^{\mathrm M}\) globally minimizes \(q\) subject to \(\|s\|_2=\Delta\), then there exists \(\lambda^{\mathrm M}\in\mathbb R\) such that \((H+\lambda^{\mathrm M}I)s^{\mathrm M}=-g\) and \(H+\lambda^{\mathrm M}I\succeq0\). If \(H+\lambda^{\mathrm M}I\succ0\), then \(s^{\mathrm M}\) is the unique global minimizer on the sphere.
statement_plain: Every global minimizer of a quadratic model on a Euclidean sphere satisfies a shifted stationarity equation with a positive-semidefinite shifted Hessian. If that shifted Hessian is positive definite, the sphere-constrained global minimizer is unique.
statement_title: Shifted-Hessian Conditions for a Sphere-Constrained Quadratic Minimizer

conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\left\{\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx:a_i^Tx=b_i\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ a_i^Tx\ge b_i\ (i\in\mathcal I)\right\}.
scope_note: Global-optimality certification for an affine-constrained QP with a positive-semidefinite Hessian.
statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(a_i^Tx=b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Let \(x^*\) be feasible and suppose there are multipliers for its active constraints such that \(Gx^*+c-\sum_{i\in\mathcal A(x^*)}\lambda_i^*a_i=0\) and \(\lambda_i^*\ge0\) for every active inequality. If \(G\succeq0\), then \(x^*\) is a global minimizer.
statement_plain: A feasible point of an affine-constrained quadratic program satisfying the KKT conditions is globally optimal when the quadratic Hessian is positive semidefinite.
statement_title: KKT sufficiency for convex quadratic programs

conclusion_latex: \operatorname{inertia}(K)=\bigl(n_+(K),n_-(K),n_0(K)\bigr).
scope_note: Foundational spectral definition used in KKT inertia results.
statement_latex: For a real symmetric matrix \(K\), let \(n_+(K)\), \(n_-(K)\), and \(n_0(K)\) be the numbers of its positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues, respectively, counted with multiplicity. The inertia of \(K\) is \[\operatorname{inertia}(K):=\bigl(n_+(K),n_-(K),n_0(K)\bigr).\]
statement_plain: The inertia of a real symmetric matrix is the triple giving its numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues.
statement_title: Inertia of a symmetric matrix

conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname{int}F\;\Longrightarrow\;Ax^*+b=0,\quad x^*=-A^{-1}b,\quad\text{and no inequality is active at }x^*.
scope_note: The strictly convex specialization of a polyhedral quadratic program and its interior-minimizer characterization.
statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Cx\le d\}\) and \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\), where \(A=A^T\succ0\), \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^m\). The problem \(\min_{x\in F}q(x)\) is a positive-definite quadratic program with linear inequalities. If a minimizer \(x^*\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}F\), no inequality is active and \(Ax^*+b=0\), so \(x^*=-A^{-1}b\).
statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic objective minimized subject to linear inequalities is a polyhedral quadratic program. If its minimizer is an interior feasible point, no constraint is active and the minimizer equals the unconstrained minimizer.
statement_title: Positive-Definite Quadratic Program with Linear Inequalities

conclusion_latex: A\succ0\iff \bigl(y^TAy>0\ \forall y\neq0\bigr).
scope_note: Full-space strict positive curvature for symmetric matrices and symmetric Hessians.
statement_latex:
A symmetric matrix \(A\) is positive definite if and only if \(y^TAy>0\) for every nonzero vector \(y\). In particular, when \(
abla^2f(x^*)\) is symmetric, \(y^T
abla^2f(x^*)y>0\) for every \(y
eq0\) is equivalent to \(
abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\).
statement_plain: A symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when its quadratic form is strictly positive in every nonzero direction. The same criterion characterizes a symmetric positive-definite Hessian.
statement_title: Positive Definiteness by the Quadratic Form

conclusion_latex: p_{\mathrm D}=\widetilde p(\tau_*),\qquad \tau_*\in\arg\min_{\substack{0\le\tau\le2\\\|\widetilde p(\tau)\|\le\Delta}}m(\widetilde p(\tau)).
scope_note: Construction of the classical dogleg approximation for a positive-definite quadratic trust-region model.
statement_latex: Let \(m(p)=f+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), where \(B\succ0\), \(g\ne0\), and \(p^{\mathrm B}=-B^{-1}g\). The exact trust-region solution is approximately \(-\Delta g/\|g\|\) for small \(\Delta\) and generally traces a curved trajectory as the radius varies. The classical dogleg method replaces that trajectory by \[p^{\mathrm U}=-\frac{g^Tg}{g^TBg}g,\qquad \widetilde p(\tau)=\begin{cases}\tau p^{\mathrm U},&0\le\tau\le1,\\p^{\mathrm U}+(\tau-1)(p^{\mathrm B}-p^{\mathrm U}),&1\le\tau\le2.\end{cases}\] It selects a point minimizing \(m\) over the portion of this path satisfying \(\|p\|\le\Delta\).
statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic model, the classical dogleg path runs from the origin to the steepest-descent line minimizer and then to the unconstrained quadratic minimizer. The dogleg step minimizes the model over the feasible part of this two-segment path, which approximates the curved exact-solution trajectory.
statement_title: Classical two-segment dogleg construction

conclusion_latex: \begin{bmatrix}P&0&G^T&A^T\\0&S^{-1}Z&I&0\\G&I&0&0\\A&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta s\\\Delta z\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_1\\S^{-1}r_2\\r_3\\r_4\end{bmatrix},\quad\text{with a reported two-step block reduction to a }2\times2\text{ block KKT system.}
scope_note: Slack-form Newton-system representation used in CVXMOD's Mehrotra predictor-corrector implementation. The reported block reduction is implementation-specific; the extract gives no convergence guarantee.
statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx\) subject to \(Gx\le h\) and \(Ax=b\), with \(P\succeq0\). Introduce \(s\ge0\) by \(Gx+s=h\), inequality multipliers \(z\ge0\), equality multipliers \(y\), and \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s)\), \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(z)\). The KKT equations are \(Px+q+G^Tz+A^Ty=0\), \(Gx+s=h\), \(Ax=b\), and \(ZS=0\). At an interior-point iterate with \(s,z>0\), their Newton linearization has coefficient matrix \[\begin{bmatrix}P&0&G^T&A^T\\0&Z&S&0\\G&I&0&0\\A&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Scaling the complementarity row by \(S^{-1}\) yields \[\begin{bmatrix}P&0&G^T&A^T\\0&S^{-1}Z&I&0\\G&I&0&0\\A&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta s\\\Delta z\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_1\\S^{-1}r_2\\r_3\\r_4\end{bmatrix}.\] CVXMOD applies two block-elimination steps to obtain a reduced \(2\times2\) block KKT system, and a Mehrotra predictor-corrector iteration solves the coefficient system with two right-hand sides.
statement_plain: For a convex QP, introducing nonnegative slacks gives primal-dual KKT equations. At an iterate with strictly positive slack and inequality-dual variables, scaling the linearized complementarity row by the inverse slack matrix produces a symmetric KKT-form Newton system. CVXMOD reduces this system by two block eliminations and uses two right-hand sides for the Mehrotra predictor and corrector computations. No convergence guarantee is asserted.
statement_title: Scaled primal-dual Newton/KKT system for a convex quadratic program

assumptions_latex: \alpha_{\tau_k}^{\mathrm{pri}},\alpha_{\tau_k}^{\mathrm{dual}}\ \text{are the fraction-to-the-boundary limits defined for the primal and dual variables}
conclusion_latex: \text{The iteration generates adaptively centered predictor-corrector QP steps while retaining strict positivity of the slack and multiplier iterates.}
scope_note: Full iteration using an affine predictor, cubic adaptive centering, the corrected direction, and a common fraction-to-the-boundary step.
statement_latex: Initialize \((x_0,y_0,\lambda_0)\) with \((y_0,\lambda_0)>0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the primal-dual Newton system with \(\sigma=0\) for \((\Delta x^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta\lambda^{\mathrm{aff}})\); set \(\mu=y^T\lambda/m\) and \[\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{aff}}=\max\{\alpha\in(0,1]:(y,\lambda)+\alpha(\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}},\Delta\lambda^{\mathrm{aff}})\ge0\},\] \[\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(y+\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta y^{\mathrm{aff}})^T(\lambda+\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{aff}}\Delta\lambda^{\mathrm{aff}})}{m},\qquad \sigma=\left(\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}}{\mu}\right)^3.\] Solve the corrected predictor-corrector system for \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta\lambda)\). Choose \(\tau_k\in(0,1)\), set \(\widehat\alpha=\min\{\alpha_{\tau_k}^{\mathrm{pri}},\alpha_{\tau_k}^{\mathrm{dual}}\}\), and update \[(x_{k+1},y_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=(x_k,y_k,\lambda_k)+\widehat\alpha(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta\lambda).\]
statement_plain: Starting from strictly positive slacks and multipliers, each iteration computes an affine predictor, estimates the complementarity attainable by that predictor, sets the centering parameter to the cube of the predicted-to-current complementarity ratio, solves the corrected system, and takes the smaller primal or dual fraction-to-the-boundary step.
statement_title: Predictor-corrector algorithm for convex quadratic programming

conclusion_latex: \forall c,\quad Z_1^{LP}\le Z_2^{LP}
scope_note: For a maximization integer program, inclusion of formulation polyhedra orders the corresponding LP upper bounds.
statement_latex: Let \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) be formulations of \(\max\{c^\top x:x\in X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\}\), and suppose \(P_1\subset P_2\). If \(Z_i^{LP}=\max\{c^\top x:x\in P_i\}\) for \(i=1,2\), then \(Z_1^{LP}\le Z_2^{LP}\) for every \(c\).
statement_plain: For a maximization integer program, an LP formulation contained in another formulation produces an LP bound no larger than the bound from the larger formulation, for every linear objective.
statement_title: Formulation Inclusion Orders LP Relaxation Bounds

conclusion_latex: x\in\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(F)\iff\exists\{(y^h,y_0^h)\}_{h\in Q^*}:\ x=\sum_{h\in Q^*}y^h,\ A^hy^h-b^hy_0^h\ge0,\ y_0^h\ge0,\ \sum_{h\in Q^*}y_0^h=1.
scope_note: Characterizes the closed convex hull of the source-defined disjunctive set using alternative-local lifted variables.
statement_latex:
In the source notation,
\[
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(F)=\left\{x:\begin{array}{l}\exists\,(y^h,y_0^h)\in\mathbb R^{n+1}\ \forall h\in Q^*,\\ x=\sum_{h\in Q^*}y^h,\quad A^hy^h-b^hy_0^h\ge 0\ \forall h\in Q^*,\\ y_0^h\ge 0\ \forall h\in Q^*,\quad \sum_{h\in Q^*}y_0^h=1\end{array}\right\}.
\]
statement_plain: A point belongs to the closed convex hull of the disjunctive set exactly when it is the sum of alternative-local vectors satisfying the corresponding homogenized systems, with nonnegative weights summing to one.
statement_title: Lifted representation of a closed disjunctive hull

assumptions_latex: (DD)\text{ and }\ell_1\text{ are defined by the surrounding quadratic-knapsack construction}
conclusion_latex: \exists\,\mu^*\text{ optimal for }(DD)\text{ such that }\ell_1(\mu^*)=0.
scope_note: The assertion depends on the surrounding definitions of the quadratic-knapsack decomposed dual $(DD)$ and the function $\ell_1$.
statement_latex: There exists an optimal solution $\mu^*$ of $(DD)$ such that $\ell_1(\mu^*)=0$.
statement_plain: The decomposed dual has at least one optimal solution at which the value of its first component function is zero.
statement_title: Optimal decomposed-dual solution with zero first component value

conclusion_latex: Ax\le b\text{ is TDI}\iff\text{conditions (i) and (ii) hold for every multiplier in their stated domains.}
scope_note: Specializes the dyadic certificate characterization by reducing its second condition to multipliers with entries in \(\{0,\tfrac12\}\) when the matrix is integral.
statement_latex: Let \(Ax\le b\) be a rational system with at least one solution, and let \(A\) be integral. It is TDI if and only if: (i) for every \(y\ge0\) with \(y^\top A\in\mathbb Z^n\), there exists a dyadic vector \(y'\ge0\) such that \({y'}^\top A=y^\top A\); and (ii) for every \(y\in\{0,\tfrac12\}^m\) with \(y^\top A\in\mathbb Z^n\), there exists \(y'\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) such that \({y'}^\top A=y^\top A\) and \({y'}^\top b\le y^\top b\).
statement_plain: For a nonempty rational system with integral A, TDI is equivalent to dyadic representability of every nonnegative multiplier producing an integral row combination, together with an integral replacement of no greater b-value for every {0, 1/2}-valued multiplier producing such a combination.
statement_title: Zero-half multiplier characterization of TDI for integral matrices

assumptions_latex: \forall i\in\mathbb N,\ P_i\text{ is a rational polyhedron}
n_i,\varphi_i\in\mathbb N\text{ are computable in time polynomially bounded by }\log i
conclusion_latex: \text{Separation is polynomially solvable when a uniform separator runs in }\operatorname{poly}(\log i,\operatorname{size}(y));\text{ optimization is defined analogously.}
scope_note: Uniform bit-complexity definition for indexed families of rational polyhedra, together with the analogous optimization definition.
statement_latex: Let \((P_i\mid i\in\mathbb N)\) be a class of rational polyhedra. Suppose that, for every \(i\), natural numbers \(n_i\) and \(\varphi_i\) can be computed in time polynomially bounded by \(\log i\), with \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) and facet complexity at most \(\varphi_i\). Separation is polynomially solvable for this class if there is one algorithm that, for every input \((i,y)\) with \(y\in\mathbb Q^{n_i}\), solves separation for \(P_i\) at \(y\) in time polynomially bounded by \(\log i\) and \(\operatorname{size}(y)\). Polynomial solvability of optimization is defined analogously by replacing separation with optimization.
statement_plain: Separation is polynomially solvable for an indexed rational-polyhedral family when its dimensions and facet-complexity bounds are efficiently computable from the index and a uniform algorithm separates every rational query point in time polynomial in the index length and query size. Optimization is defined analogously.
statement_title: Polynomially solvable separation for an indexed polyhedral family

assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a rational polyhedron}
conclusion_latex: \alpha'x\leq\beta'\text{ dominates }\alpha x\leq\beta\iff P\cap\{x:\alpha'x\leq\beta'\}\subset P\cap\{x:\alpha x\leq\beta\}
scope_note: Retains only the explicit terminology introduced by the composite extract; the separately stated polyhedrality theorem is not merged into this definition.
statement_latex: \text{A split inequality }\alpha'x\leq\beta'\text{ dominates a split inequality }\alpha x\leq\beta\text{ relative to }P\text{ if }P\cap\{x:\alpha'x\leq\beta'\}\subset P\cap\{x:\alpha x\leq\beta\}.\text{ A split inequality is undominated if it is not dominated by any split inequality.}
statement_plain: A split inequality dominates another when imposing it on P produces a strict subset of the region obtained by imposing the other inequality. A split inequality is undominated when no split inequality dominates it.
statement_title: Dominated and undominated split inequalities

conclusion_latex: A\text{ is unimodular}\iff\left(A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n},\ \operatorname{rank}(A)=m,\ \det(B)\in\{0,\pm1\}\text{ for every }m\times m\text{ submatrix }B\right)
scope_note: Defines rectangular full-row-rank unimodularity through maximal minors and records the square-matrix specialization.
statement_latex: An \(m\times n\) matrix \(A\) is unimodular if and only if it is integral, \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), and every \(m\times m\) submatrix \(B\) satisfies \(\det(B)\in\{0,\pm1\}\). In particular, a square matrix \(U\) is unimodular if and only if it is integral and \(\det(U)=\pm1\).
statement_plain: A matrix is unimodular when it is integral, has full row rank, and every maximal minor is zero or plus or minus one. For a square matrix, this is equivalent to integrality and determinant plus or minus one.
statement_title: Unimodular matrix

conclusion_latex: \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,l\}:\quad \mu^{j+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m}\widehat D^j(\mu).
scope_note: Extraction-grounded unlocalized multiplier-search iteration using successive polyhedral dual approximations.
statement_latex:
Choose \(\mu^1\in\mathbb R_+^m\). For \(j=1,\ldots,l\), compute \(g(\mu^j)\) and \(D(\mu^j)\), and select
\[
\mu^{j+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m}\widehat D^j(\mu).
\]
statement_plain: Start with a nonnegative multiplier. At each of l iterations, evaluate the dual function and a subgradient at the current multiplier, then choose the next multiplier as a maximizer of the current polyhedral dual approximation over the nonnegative orthant.
statement_title: Dual cutting-plane algorithm

conclusion_latex: W_k^{j+1}=W_k^j\cup\{w_k\}\quad(k=1,\ldots,p;\ j=1,\ldots,l)
scope_note: Finite prescribed-iteration scheme that repeatedly solves a feasible restricted master and adds one pricing solution for each component.
statement_latex: Initialize finite sets \(W_k^1\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(G_k)\), \(k=1,\ldots,p\), such that RMP (4.16) is feasible. For \(j=1,\ldots,l\), compute dual and primal solutions \(\mu^j\) and \(z^j\) of (4.16). For each \(k=1,\ldots,p\), compute a solution \(w_k\) of (4.17) and set \[W_k^{j+1}=W_k^j\cup\{w_k\}.\]
statement_plain: Start with component column sets that make the restricted master feasible. At each prescribed iteration, solve the restricted master, solve one pricing problem per component, and add each resulting point to its component set.
statement_title: Restricted-Master Column Generation for Structured MINLP

conclusion_latex: \mu^{j+1}=\Pi\!\left(\mu^j-\alpha^j g^j/\lVert g^j\rVert\right)
scope_note: Finite projected subgradient iteration for nonnegative Lagrangian multiplier vectors; the displayed normalized update is defined only when the evaluated subgradient is nonzero.
statement_latex: Choose \(\mu^1\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\). For \(j=1,\ldots,l\), set \(g^j=g(\mu^j)\) and, whenever \(\lVert g^j\rVert>0\), update \[\mu^{j+1}=\Pi\!\left(\mu^j-\alpha^j\frac{g^j}{\lVert g^j\rVert}\right).\]
statement_plain: Start from a nonnegative multiplier vector. At each of finitely many iterations, evaluate the subgradient, take a normalized step, and project. The extract supplies no stopping convention for a zero subgradient, for which the displayed division is undefined.
statement_title: Normalized Projected Subgradient Iteration

conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ pairwise disjoint cuts }\mathcal D\text{ of }G\text{ such that }\left|\{D\in\mathcal D:D\text{ separates }s,t\}\right|=\operatorname{dist}_G(s,t)\quad\forall st\in R.
scope_note: Cut representation associated with bipartite supply graphs whose supply–demand union is planar.
statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) and \(H=(V,R)\) be graphs such that \(G\) is bipartite and \(G+H\) is planar. Then there is a family of pairwise disjoint cuts of \(G\) such that, for every demand edge \(r=st\in R\), the vertices \(s\) and \(t\) are separated by exactly \(\operatorname{dist}_G(s,t)\) cuts in the family.
statement_plain: If the supply graph is bipartite and its union with the demand graph is planar, there are disjoint supply cuts such that each demand pair is separated by exactly its graph distance many cuts.
statement_title: Disjoint-cut distance representation in planar bipartite supply graphs

conclusion_latex: A\text{ is NP-complete}
scope_note: Sufficient condition for proving NP-completeness through polynomial-time reduction from an NP-complete problem.
statement_latex: If \(A\in\mathrm{NP}\), \(B\) is NP-complete, and \(B\preccurlyeq A\), then \(A\) is NP-complete.
statement_plain: If A is in NP, B is NP-complete, and B polynomial-time reduces to A, then A is NP-complete.
statement_title: NP-Completeness Transfer by Reduction

assumptions_latex: \text{The machines are identical and the objective is makespan minimization.}
\text{Jobs are ordered by nonincreasing processing time and then list-scheduled.}
conclusion_latex: C_{\max}^{\mathrm{LPT}}\le \frac{4}{3}C_{\max}^{\star}
scope_note: Approximation guarantee for LPT makespan scheduling on identical parallel machines.
statement_latex: For scheduling jobs on identical parallel machines to minimize makespan, the longest processing time rule is a \(\frac{4}{3}\)-approximation algorithm.
statement_plain: The longest processing time rule is a 4/3-approximation for minimizing makespan on identical parallel machines.
statement_title: Four-Thirds Approximation of LPT

assumptions_latex: G\text{ is an undirected Eulerian graph}
conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ an orientation }\vec G\text{ of }G\text{ such that }\vec G\text{ is directed Eulerian}
scope_note: Existence of an orientation producing a directed Eulerian graph.
statement_latex: Every undirected Eulerian graph \(G\) admits an orientation \(\vec G\) that is a directed Eulerian graph.
statement_plain: Every undirected Eulerian graph can be oriented so that the resulting directed graph is Eulerian.
statement_title: Eulerian orientation of an undirected Eulerian graph

assumptions_latex: \text{Each elementary rule is a function of job and/or machine attributes.}
\text{Each elementary rule has an associated scaling parameter.}
conclusion_latex: \text{The scaled elementary rules form a ranking expression used to generate a schedule.}
scope_note: Deterministic-scheduling ranking expression assembled from elementary job- or machine-attribute rules.
statement_latex: A composite dispatching rule is a ranking expression combining elementary dispatching rules. Each elementary rule is a function of constant or time-dependent job or machine attributes and has its own scaling parameter. A scaling parameter may be fixed or may vary with time or with the job set. Job-set-dependent parameters are obtained by applying predetermined functions to instance statistics, which usually do not depend on the schedule. For each instance, the required statistics are computed, the scaling parameters are set, and the resulting ranking expression is applied to generate a schedule.
statement_plain: A composite dispatching rule combines elementary ranking rules based on job or machine attributes. Each component has a scaling parameter that may be fixed, time-dependent, or determined from instance statistics. These statistics usually do not depend on the schedule; predetermined functions map them to parameter values before the combined rule is applied.
statement_title: Composite dispatching rule

assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a nonempty proper modular cut of }M
\text{For the general definition, }N\text{ is a matroid and }X\subseteq E(N)
conclusion_latex: (M+_{\mathcal M}e)/e\text{ is an elementary quotient of rank }r(M)-1;\quad Q\text{ is a quotient of }M\iff \exists N,X:\ M=N\setminus X,\ Q=N/X.
scope_note: Defines general and elementary matroid quotients and records the excluded trivial modular-cut cases.
statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid and let \(\mathcal M\) be a nonempty proper modular cut of \(M\). The elementary quotient of \(M\) with respect to \(\mathcal M\) is \((M+_{\mathcal M}e)/e\); it has ground set \(E(M)\) and rank \(r(M)-1\). More generally, \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) if there exist a matroid \(N\) and a set \(X\subseteq E(N)\) such that \(M=N\setminus X\) and \(Q=N/X\). Consequently, \(E(Q)=E(M)\). If \(\mathcal M\) is empty or is the set of all flats of \(M\), the elementary construction instead returns \(M\).
statement_plain: An elementary quotient is obtained by extending a matroid using a nonempty proper modular cut and then contracting the new element; it preserves the ground set and lowers rank by one. In general, Q is a quotient of M when deleting a set X from some matroid N gives M while contracting X gives Q. Empty or nonproper modular cuts produce only the trivial result M.
statement_title: Matroid quotients and elementary quotients

assumptions_latex: I\text{ is any instance of the online scheduling problem}
F\text{ is the objective being minimized}
conclusion_latex: F_A(I)\leq \rho\,\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{off}}(I)\quad\text{for every }I.
scope_note: Competitive performance for a minimization objective relative to an optimal offline schedule.
statement_latex: An online scheduling algorithm $A$ is $\rho$-competitive if, for every instance $I$, its objective value satisfies $F_A(I)\leq \rho\,\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{off}}(I)$, where $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{off}}(I)$ is the optimal value attainable when all problem data are known beforehand.
statement_plain: An online scheduling algorithm is rho-competitive if its objective value on every instance is at most rho times the optimal offline value obtained with all data known in advance.
statement_title: Competitive ratio of an online scheduling algorithm

conclusion_latex: \alpha=1\Longrightarrow x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f
scope_note: Proximity-based scaling method for an M-convex function with bounded effective domain.
statement_latex: Let f be M-convex with bounded effective domain and K_\infty=\max\{\lVert p-q\rVert_\infty:p,q\in\operatorname{dom}f\}. Choose x\in\operatorname{dom}f, set \alpha=2^{\lceil\log_2(K_\infty/(4n))\rceil} and B=\operatorname{dom}f. At each scale, use steepest descent initialized at 0 to find an integer vector y locally minimizing \widetilde f(y)=f(x+\alpha y) when x+\alpha y\in B and +\infty otherwise, and set x\leftarrow x+\alpha y. If \alpha=1, return x. Otherwise set B\leftarrow B\cap\{z\in\mathbf{Z}^{V}:\lVert z-x\rVert_\infty\leq(n-1)(\alpha-1)\}, set \alpha\leftarrow\alpha/2, and repeat. The returned x is a minimizer of f.
statement_plain: At each scale, solve a rescaled restricted problem by exchange steepest descent, update the current point, restrict the retained domain to the prescribed proximity box, and halve the scale. At scale one, the current point is a global minimizer.
statement_title: Steepest-Descent Scaling Algorithm for M-Convex Minimization

assumptions_latex: \text{each connected component contains an even number of vertices of }T\triangle T'
conclusion_latex: J\triangle N\text{ is a minimum-cost }T\text{-join for the original }(c,T).
scope_note: Constructive minimum-cost T-join algorithm using a negative-edge parity transformation and metric-closure matching.
statement_latex: Let N=\{e\in E:c_e<0\} and T'=\{v\in V:|\delta(v)\cap N|\text{ is odd}\}. Replace (c,T) by (|c|,T\triangle T'). For every pair u,v in the transformed T, compute a minimum-cost u-v path P_{uv} of cost d(u,v). Find a minimum-weight perfect matching M in the complete graph on T with weights d(u,v), let J=\triangle_{uv\in M}E(P_{uv}), and return J\triangle N.
statement_plain: Toggle the required odd-degree vertices by the odd-degree boundary of the negative-cost edges, replace costs by their absolute values, compute shortest paths between the transformed terminals, and find a minimum-weight perfect matching in the resulting metric closure. The symmetric difference of the matched paths, toggled by the original negative edges, is an optimal T-join.
statement_title: Optimal T-Join via Shortest Paths and Perfect Matching

assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is a capacitated graph in the setting of the Gomory--Hu procedure}
\text{a selected tree part contains two terminal nodes}
conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure terminates when every node of }T\text{ contains exactly one terminal of }K,\text{ with every tree edge assigned a cut-capacity label }f_e.
scope_note: Iterative construction for a capacitated graph and designated terminal set.
statement_latex: Choose terminals $r,s\in K$, compute a minimum $(r,s)$-cut with shores $R,S$, and initialize a tree whose nodes are $R,S$ and whose joining edge is labeled by the cut capacity. At a later stage, if a tree node $A$ contains terminals $y,z\in K$, form $G_A$ by identifying, separately, the vertices represented by each component of $T-A$. Compute a minimum $(y,z)$-cut in $G_A$, split $A$ into its shores $Y,Z$, join $Y$ and $Z$ by an edge labeled by that cut's capacity, and reattach each former neighbor of $A$ to the shore containing its identified vertex; retain all old edge labels. Continue until every tree node contains exactly one terminal.
statement_plain: Start with a minimum cut between two terminals. Repeatedly split a tree part containing two terminals by a minimum cut after separately identifying the external tree components. Add the corresponding labeled edge, reattach neighboring parts according to their cut shores, and retain existing labels. Stop when every tree part contains one terminal.
statement_title: Gomory–Hu Cut-Tree Construction

conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) has a solution in \(\mathbb{Z}^n\) exactly under the displayed divisibility and zero conditions.
scope_note: Smith-normal-form criterion for solvability of linear Diophantine systems.
statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\), let \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and let unimodular matrices \(U\) and \(V\) satisfy \(UAV=D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_r,0,\ldots)\), where \(d_i>0\) and \(d_i\mid d_{i+1}\). With \(c=Ub\), the system \(Ax=b\) has a solution in \(\mathbb{Z}^n\) if and only if \(d_i\mid c_i\) for every \(1\le i\le r\) and \(c_i=0\) for every \(r<i\le m\).
statement_plain: Smith normal form reduces integer linear-system feasibility exactly to divisibility conditions on the nonzero diagonal coordinates and zero conditions on the remaining transformed right-hand-side coordinates.
statement_title: Diophantine Constraint Reasoning

assumptions_latex: \text{all machines are idle just before }t_1\text{ and immediately after }t_2
conclusion_latex: \exists\sigma^*\text{ optimal for all }n\text{ jobs such that }\sigma^*\text{ and }\sigma\text{ agree between }t_1\text{ and }t_2
scope_note: A dominance principle under which an isolated feasible interval schedule can be preserved within an overall optimum.
statement_latex: Suppose there is a feasible schedule \(\sigma\) for \(J_{[t_1,t_2]}\), all machines are idle just before \(t_1\) and immediately after \(t_2\), and every job in \(J_{[t_1,t_2]}\) is on time. Then there exists an overall optimal schedule \(\sigma^*\) for all \(n\) jobs such that \(\sigma^*\) and \(\sigma\) agree between \(t_1\) and \(t_2\).
statement_plain: If a job set has a feasible, entirely on-time schedule isolated by machine idleness at both ends of an interval, then some optimal schedule for all jobs preserves that interval schedule.
statement_title: Embedding an Isolated On-Time Interval Schedule

assumptions_latex: The selected representative of \(\Gamma\) is a core.
conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\in\mathrm{P}\).
scope_note: Algebraic tractability side of the finite-domain CSP dichotomy.
statement_latex: Let \(D\) be finite and let \(\Gamma\) be a finite constraint language on \(D\). Replace \(\Gamma\) by a core having the same CSP complexity. If this core admits a Taylor polymorphism—equivalently, an idempotent Siggers polymorphism—then the decision problem \(\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\), whose input is a conjunction of constraints using relations from \(\Gamma\), is solvable in polynomial time.
statement_plain: A finite constraint language is polynomial-time tractable when its core admits a Taylor, equivalently idempotent Siggers, polymorphism.
statement_title: Finite-Language Tractable Side

assumptions_latex: \(g=\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\), with not all \(a_i\) equal to zero.
conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\in\mathbb{Z}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i=b\iff g\mid b\).
scope_note: Exact gcd criterion for one linear Diophantine equation.
statement_latex: For \(a_1,\ldots,a_n,b\in\mathbb{Z}\), with not all \(a_i\) zero, let \(g=\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\). Then there exists \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i=b\) if and only if \(g\mid b\).
statement_plain: An integer linear equation is solvable exactly when the gcd of its coefficients divides its right-hand side.
statement_title: Divisibility Constraint Reasoning

assumptions_latex: The selected representative of \(\Gamma\) is a core.
conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\) is NP-complete.
scope_note: Algebraic hardness side of the finite-domain CSP dichotomy.
statement_latex: Let \(D\) be finite and let \(\Gamma\) be a finite constraint language on \(D\). Replace \(\Gamma\) by a core having the same CSP complexity. If this core has no Taylor polymorphism—equivalently, no idempotent Siggers polymorphism—then \(\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\) is NP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
statement_plain: A finite constraint language is NP-complete when its core has no Taylor, equivalently no idempotent Siggers, polymorphism.
statement_title: Finite-Language Hard Side

assumptions_latex: \text{The two job chains are adjacent in the schedule sequence.}
conclusion_latex: \text{Their interchange is an adjacent sequence interchange and generalizes adjacent pairwise interchange.}
scope_note: Terminology for a local transformation of two neighboring job chains in a schedule sequence.
statement_latex: An \emph{adjacent sequence interchange} is an interchange of two adjacent chains of jobs. It generalizes an adjacent pairwise interchange.
statement_plain: An adjacent sequence interchange swaps two adjacent job chains and generalizes an adjacent pairwise interchange.
statement_title: Adjacent Sequence Interchange

conclusion_latex: G'=(V,E')\text{ is a tree}\iff G'\text{ is a connected forest}
scope_note: Definition for a subgraph on the full vertex set.
statement_latex: Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ and $E'\subseteq E$, the subgraph $G'=(V,E')$ is a tree if it is a forest and is connected, meaning that it contains a path between every pair of vertices in $V$.
statement_plain: A spanning subgraph is a tree when it is cycle-free and connected, so every pair of vertices is joined by a path.
statement_title: Spanning Tree

assumptions_latex: \text{Integrality enforcement has higher priority than quadratic-constraint enforcement}
conclusion_latex: \operatorname{enforce}(\widetilde x):\quad \text{forward propagation}\to\text{separation if not pruned}\to\text{spatial branching if not separated}.
scope_note: MIQCP-specific specialization of the general CIP constraint-enforcement service.
statement_latex: During enforcement, a constraint handler checks the current LP solution \(\widetilde x\) and may resolve a violation by adding a separating cut, tightening a variable bound so that \(\widetilde x\) is excluded from the current domain, pruning the node, or branching. Under the stated SCIP priority configuration, integrality constraints are enforced before quadratic constraints, so all integer variables are integral when quadratic enforcement processes the LP optimum. For a violated quadratic constraint, first perform forward propagation; if it does not prove infeasibility, invoke separation; if separation does not exclude \(\widetilde x\), perform spatial branching.
statement_plain: Constraint enforcement may cut, tighten bounds, prune, or branch. With integrality enforcement assigned higher priority, integer variables are integral before quadratic feasibility is enforced. A violated quadratic constraint is then processed by forward propagation, followed by separation and finally spatial branching if the preceding steps do not resolve it.
statement_title: Quadratic-Constraint Enforcement Sequence

assumptions_latex: \forall x\text{ feasible},\ \bigl(x^l(k)\le x\le x^u(k),\ x^l(k)\to x,\ x^u(k)\to x\bigr)\Rightarrow\bigl(P_1\{x^l(k),x^u(k)\}\to0\ \lor\ P_2\{z^l(k),z^u(k)\}\to0\bigr)
conclusion_latex: \overline{\{x_k\}}=[a,b],\qquad \operatorname{Acc}(\{x_k^{\min}\})\subseteq X^\star
scope_note: Convergence guarantee for the corresponding RPAS-type algorithm using a decomposable multiplicative diagonal partition operator.
statement_latex: Let f be continuous on [a,b], and let P=P_1\{x^l,x^u\}P_2\{z^l,z^u\} be a decomposable multiplicative diagonal partition operator. Assume that for every feasible x and every sequence x^l(k)\le x\le x^u(k) with x^l(k)\to x and x^u(k)\to x, either P_1\{x^l(k),x^u(k)\}\to0 or P_2\{f(x^l(k)),f(x^u(k))\}\to0. Then the corresponding RPAS-type algorithm generates an everywhere-dense set in [a,b], and every accumulation point of its minimizer-point sequence belongs to X^\star.
statement_plain: For a continuous objective, if at least one factor of the multiplicatively decomposed operator tends to zero whenever an enclosing feasible box shrinks to a point, the corresponding RPAS-type algorithm generates a dense set and every accumulation point of its minimizer sequence is globally optimal.
statement_title: Density and Global-Optimality Limit Property for Multiplicative Diagonal Partition Search

conclusion_latex: \beta(M)\leq\psi(y)\ \text{for every }y\in Q(D)\cap M\text{ with }\varphi(y)\leq0;\qquad \omega(M)=U\bar t(M)\text{ lies on an edge of }M\Rightarrow\beta(M)=\min\{\psi(y)\mid y\in Q(D)\cap M,\ \varphi(y)\leq0\}.
scope_note: Lower-bound validity and its edge-based exactness condition in parametric decomposition.
statement_latex: The quantity \(\beta(M)\) is a lower bound for \(\psi(y)\) over the feasible points in \(M\). If \(\omega(M)=U\bar t(M)\) lies on an edge of \(M\), then \[\beta(M)=\min\{\psi(y)\mid y\in Q(D)\cap M,\ \varphi(y)\leq0\}.\]
statement_plain: The regional quantity beta(M) lower-bounds the objective on the feasible points in M. If the designated point omega(M) lies on an edge of M, the bound equals the regional feasible minimum.
statement_title: Validity and edge exactness of the regional bound

assumptions_latex: S\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty and closed}
h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is strictly convex}
conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall x\in S,\ d(x)=0\bigr)\land\bigl(\forall x\notin S,\ d(x)>0\bigr)\land\bigl(x^k\to x,\ d(x^k)\to0\Rightarrow x\in S\bigr)
scope_note: Characterizes membership in the closed set using the separation functional defined from a strictly convex function.
statement_latex:
Let \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be strictly convex, and let \(d\geq0\) be determined by
\[
d^2(x)=\inf_{\substack{y\in S\\p\in\partial h(x)}}\bigl[h(y)-h(x)-\langle p,y-x\rangle\bigr].
\]
Then \(d(x)=0\) for every \(x\in S\), \(d(x)>0\) for every \(x\notin S\), and, whenever \(x^k\to x\) and \(d(x^k)\to0\), one has \(x\in S\).
statement_plain: The separation functional vanishes on S, is strictly positive outside S, and detects membership at limits of convergent sequences whose functional values approach zero.
statement_title: Zero-Set and Sequential Detection Properties of the Separation Functional

conclusion_latex: \mathbf h\text{ is the }G\text{-steepest-descent vector field associated with }b\text{ on }\mathcal F\cap\widetilde\Gamma
scope_note: Specialized geometric characterization of the ODE field used in the constrained quadratic-optimization formulation.
statement_latex: The vector field \(\mathbf h(\mathbf x)\) defined by (28), restricted to \(\mathcal F\cap\widetilde\Gamma\), is the steepest-descent vector field associated with \(b(\mathbf x)=\mathbf c^T\mathbf x\) under the Riemannian metric \(G(\mathbf x)=X^{-1}=\operatorname{Diag}(\mathbf x^{-1})=\operatorname{Diag}(\mu^{-1},w_1^{-1},\ldots,w_n^{-1},\xi^{-1})\), which is defined on the positive orthant \(\widetilde\Gamma\).
statement_plain: On the feasible portion of the positive orthant, the specified ODE field is the Riemannian steepest-descent field for the linear objective under the inverse-coordinate diagonal metric.
statement_title: Riemannian steepest-descent representation of the vector field

assumptions_latex: \operatorname{Dual}(7.1)\text{ is the dual problem associated with formulation }(7.1)
conclusion_latex: \underline v_{\mathrm{dual}}:=\operatorname{val}(\operatorname{Dual}(7.1)),\qquad \forall\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m:\ \underline v_{\mathrm{dual}}\geq D(\mu),\qquad \underline v_{\mathrm{dual}}\geq\underline v_{\mathrm{MINLP}}.
scope_note: Defines the optimized dual value associated with formulation (7.1) and records its dominance over each dual-function value and the stated MINLP lower bound.
statement_latex: For the dual problem associated with formulation \((7.1)\), define \(\underline v_{\mathrm{dual}}:=\operatorname{val}(\operatorname{Dual}(7.1))\). Then \(\underline v_{\mathrm{dual}}\geq D(\mu)\) for every \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \(\underline v_{\mathrm{dual}}\geq\underline v_{\mathrm{MINLP}}\).
statement_plain: The dual bound is the optimal value of the dual problem associated with formulation (7.1). It is at least every dual-function value for a nonnegative multiplier and is at least the stated MINLP lower bound.
statement_title: Optimized Dual Global Bound

M\subseteq igcup_{i\in I}M_i,\quad M_i\cap M
eq\varnothing\ ( orall i\in I),\quad M_j
subseteq igcup_{\substack{i\in I\i
eq j}}M_i\ ( orall j\in I)
scope_note: Defines a full-dimensional, irredundant simplicial cover of a simplex.
statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be an \(n\)-dimensional simplex. A simplicial cover \(\mathcal C_M=\{M_i:i\in I\}\) of \(M\) is a collection of \(n\)-dimensional simplices such that \(M\subseteq igcup_{i\in I}M_i\), \(M_i\cap M
eq\varnothing\) for every \(i\in I\), and \(M_j
